articles.title: Lane Kiffin sorry for profanity use during halftime interview in loss to Tennessee: 'No excuses'
articles.summary: The Tigers have now lost three straight games and sit at just 6-5 on the year entering Saturday's regular-season finale.
articles.body:
Lane Kiffin apologized Monday for his on-air outburst at halftime of LSU's 27-13 loss to No. 9 Tennessee last weekend.

The Tigers head coach used explicit language while speaking with the LSU Sports Radio Network at halftime of that loss in Knoxville. Kiffin was upset after Tigers safety Ty Benefield was ejected for targeting while tackling Tennessee tight end DaSaahn Brame in the final minute of the half. That ended up leading to a touchdown, which put Tennessee up 10-6 at the break.

"Obviously, we played really well defensively," Kiffin said at halftime, via ESPN . "We started well offensively. Bad punt, really poor in the red zone. So, we have to come back, have to move the ball better on offense, and not get a f***ing bulls**t targeting call."

Kiffin apologized for his language on Monday.

"No excuses. I was frustrated with the first half and really couldn't even hear the question, kind of like our center down in the student section," he said. "But there's no reason for that. And so, to the people who were offended, I apologize for that."

The Tigers have now lost three straight games and sit at just 6-5 this fall. Kiffin signed a seven-year, $91 million deal to jump to LSU last fall after an impressive run with Ole Miss. But he's now just the first coach to lose five games in his inaugural season at LSU since 1991.

The Tigers will close the regular season on Saturday against Arkansas. A loss there would give them their worst record since 2021, when they went 6-7 in the final year of Ed Orgeron's tenure.

"People say, 'What's the problem with this season, and are you really concerned about the program?'" Kiffin said on Monday. "And I keep saying, 'I'm not concerned about the future of the program. I'm excited about the future of the program, but we have one core issue to fix, and that's how we finish games. We're in these games against really, really good teams, and we don't play well late, and that can be part of a mindset that we don't have right."

articles.title: How Glenn Schumann Becoming FSU HC Impacts Georgia's CFP Championship Pursuit
articles.summary: The next era of Florida State football is officially underway after it hired Georgia defensive coordinator Glenn Schumann as its next head coach on Monday, but the Bulldogs also have a national championship to win.
articles.body:
The next era of Florida State football is officially underway after it hired Georgia defensive coordinator Glenn Schumann as its next head coach on Monday, but the Bulldogs also have a national championship to win.

And he plans on helping them do just that before moving to his next role.

ESPN's Andrea Adelson reported Monday that Schumann is expected to stay with the SEC program through the regular season and postseason. He has a long relationship with Georgia head coach Kirby Smart, as he followed him from Alabama to the Bulldogs in 2016 and has remained on his staff.

As for Florida State, the position was open because school president Richard McCullough announced on Nov. 1 following a loss to Clemson that he fired Mike Norvell.

ESPN's Pete Thamel reported at the time the school owed Norvell a $50.3 million buyout, although that number was subject to offset language.

"According to the contract, Norvell is obligated to mitigate and seek a market-rate salary immediately upon being terminated," Dan Rorabaugh of the Tallahassee Democrat reported. "If he gets a new job, the amount owed by FSU would be reduced by the amount of Norvell's new salary. That's the same stipulation that got James Franklin's buyout from Penn State lowered from $49 million to $9 million when he got the Virginia Tech job."

While things ended poorly under Norvell, Florida State is still a traditional powerhouse playing in an ACC that is not exactly loaded with elite-level competition outside of Miami at this point. That was surely enticing to a number of potential candidates, and it will be up to Schumann to direct a turnaround.

What's more, the College Football Playoff expanding means there will be even more opportunity to accomplish postseason goals if the Seminoles elevate themselves above the middle of the pack in the conference.

The blueprint is there, as it wasn't long ago Florida State went undefeated in the 2023 regular season before losing the Orange Bowl without injured quarterback Jordan Travis.

Yet that Orange Bowl loss set off a troubling slide for the program under Norvell, as it went 2-10 the next season and 5-7 during the 2025 campaign. It also started 3-5 overall and 1-4 in ACC play during the 2026 season when it decided to fire Norvell.

Schumann is undoubtedly facing a rebuilding process after the past few years.

However, rebuilding is something that can be done much faster in the modern era of college football thanks to the transfer portal. Coaches are no longer solely reliant on high school recruiting and hoping young players make an immediate impact, and Florida State has a history of success its new leader can point to when searching for new players.

Schumann is also accustomed to competing at the highest level of the sport from his time with Georgia.

He started with the Bulldogs in 2016 as an inside linebackers coach, became the co-defensive coordinator in 2019 and then took over as the defensive coordinator in 2022.

Georgia's defense is a major reason it has been among college football's best programs throughout the past decade, including when it won back-to-back national championships during the 2021 and 2022 seasons.

Florida State is something of a sleeping giant in the ACC and is surely striving to reach that level, especially with more CFP spots up for grabs in the immediate future. It is now up to Schumann to figure out a way to maximize the program's potential after a troubling stretch to end Norvell's tenure.

First, though, he will look to help lead the No. 1 team in the College Football Playoff rankings to another national title.

articles.title: Otro Van Nistelrooy en Valdebebas
articles.standfirst: Liam Van Nistelrooy, hijo del mítico Ruud y delantero como él, visita hoy el Di Stéfano con el PSV para disputar la Youth League
articles.summary: Liam Van Nistelrooy, hijo del mítico Ruud y delantero como él, visita hoy el Di Stéfano con el PSV para disputar la Youth League
articles.body: El primer gol de Liam Van Nistelrooy en esta Youth League fue un calco de los que hacía su padre Ruud. Dyran Stam (hijo de también de ex jugador, Ronnie) disparó, el portero del Shakhtar rechazó el balón y Liam estaba allí para empujarlo. Fue el único tanto del partido. Este martes, el delantero del PSV visita al Juvenil A del Real Madrid en el Alfredo Di Stéfano (16.00 horas). Liam es un delantero puro, un rematador que no necesita muchos minutos para hacerse notar y que también juega bien al espacio. La Youth le cuenta cuatro goles en 91 minutos, a razón de uno cada 23, y apenas cinco disparos en tres partidos. Al tanto contra el Shakhtar le siguió un doblete saliendo del banquillo en el 1-6 al Leipzig. Ante el Brujas entró en el minuto 85, con 2-2, y en el 87 marcó el gol de la victoria. En dos de las tres jornadas que ha disputado, el PSV ha ganado por la mínima gracias a un gol suyo. El partido reúne a dos clubes en los que su padre Ruud van Nistelrooy dejó huella. En Eindhoven se dio a conocer como uno de los grandes goleadores de Europa y sus datos, 62 tantos en 67 partidos de Liga entre 1998 y 200, le valieron para llamar la atención de los grandes. De allí salió rumbo al Manchester United y a Eindhoven ya solo volvió como entrenador. Pasó por el filial antes de dirigir al primer equipo en la temporada 2022-23, en la que ganó la Copa y la Supercopa neerlandesas. Al Bernabéu llegó en 2006, con 30 años, y en su primera temporada fue Pichichi con 25 goles y campeón de Liga. Al año siguiente volvió a ganarla. En total, 64 tantos en 96 partidos de blanco, dos Ligas y una Supercopa de España. Uno de los mejores delanteros centro de la historia y uno de los más queridos por la afición madridista, que todavía recuerda cómo remataba. Veinte años después de la llegada de Ruud al Real Madrid, su hijo se presenta en Valdebebas con la camiseta del PSV y el dorsal 55. El apellido hará que todos se fijen en él desde el calentamiento.

articles.title: Rafa Cruz, la sonrisa canaria que ya es historia de España: "Ni en el recreo lo había logrado"
articles.standfirst: El joven extremo de Las Palmas iguala el récord de contribuciones directas de gol en un partido oficial con la selección española masculina, contando todas sus categorías, desde que existen registros estadísticos
articles.summary: El joven extremo de Las Palmas iguala el récord de contribuciones directas de gol en un partido oficial con la selección española masculina, contando todas sus categorías, desde que existen registros estadísticos
articles.body: Hay una sonrisa en Catar que merece detenerse a observar. La de un chico de 17 años. Canario. De esos futbolistas que parecen encontrar en el balón una extensión de su felicidad. Rafa Cruz, dueño de una tarde que el fútbol español tardará en olvidar, atendió a MARCA con el trofeo de mejor jugador del partido entre las manos y el desparpajo de quien todavía no había terminado de asimilar lo que acababa de hacer. Cinco goles, dos asistencias y un pedazo de historia. Todo en 70 minutos. "Creo que nunca lo había logrado", reconocía entre sonrisas cuando se le preguntaba si, quizá en alguna de aquellas mañanas de fútbol en el patio del colegio, había conseguido marcar cinco goles. Ni siquiera allí. Ha tenido que viajar desde Gran Canaria hasta Catar y enfundarse la camiseta de España en un Mundial para presentarse al mundo. Y, de paso, hacer algo que ningún futbolista había conseguido en la historia de la competición masculina sub-17. Necesitó cinco minutos para estrenar su cuenta, diez para firmar un doblete y 21 para completar un 'hat-trick'. Después del descanso llegaron los otros dos tantos. Entre medias, un par de asistencias. Una intervención directa en un gol cada diez minutos que le sitúa a la altura de la extraordinaria actuación que protagonizó Carlos Espí, apenas 53 días antes, con la selección española sub-21 ante San Marino. Cinco goles y dos asistencias también para el delantero madridista. Dos exhibiciones con idéntica firma estadística que representan el mayor registro localizado en un partido de competición oficial de las selecciones españolas masculinas con los datos de goles y asistencias disponibles. La dimensión histórica del repóker invita a viajar hasta 1934, cuando Isidro Lángara, delantero del Real Oviedo, anotó cinco de los nueve goles que España le endosó a Portugal en la clasificación para el Mundial de Italia. Más de nueve décadas después, un adolescente canario ha encontrado su propio lugar en la memoria goleadora de las selecciones españolas. "Me ha beneficiado mucho el plan de partido del míster y el trabajo de todos los compañeros. Ha sido una locura. Todos son especiales y creo que, si seguimos así, podemos conseguir ganar el Mundial", explicaba el protagonista, empeñado en repartir los méritos de una actuación que, inevitablemente, lleva su nombre. Hay una seña que explica a Rafa Cruz mejor que cualquiera de sus cinco goles. Apenas habían transcurrido cinco minutos cuando, después de inaugurar el marcador, el extremo mostró la camiseta de Christian Imga, obligado a abandonar la concentración por lesión. En el día que quedará registrado como el de su mayor exhibición goleadora, su primer recuerdo fue para quien ya no podía estar allí. "Fue una pena increíble porque ya nos había pasado con Enzo antes de venir a Catar. Era un hermano que teníamos aquí", confesaba a MARCA. Una dedicatoria acompañada de un mensaje de cariño para su compañero. España se marchó al descanso con nueve goles de ventaja y regresó al césped con el mismo apetito. El camino de Rafa Cruz en el fútbol tiene un compañero de viaje inseparable: Jorge, su hermano gemelo. Comparten posición, características futbolísticas y un sueño que empieza a tomar forma. Poco antes de cumplir los 17 años, los gemelos Cruz ya llegaron a compartir convocatoria con el primer equipo amarillo de la mano de Rubén de la Barrera el pasado octubre. Poco antes, durante el mes agosto, todavía con 16 años, Rafa debutó con el primer equipo amarillo ante el Albacete. Lo hizo sustituyendo a Jesé Rodríguez. Una curiosa coincidencia entre dos futbolistas canarios que conocen los pasillos de Valdebebas. Y es que Rafa pasó una temporada en la cantera del Real Madrid y, tras ella, emprendió el camino de vuelta a casa. La cantera de la UD Las Palmas, tierra fértil para el talento, vuelve a ofrecer al fútbol español motivos para ilusionarse. Rafa ha crecido mirando a quienes recorrieron antes ese camino. "Me fijo mucho en Pedri y Moleiro, son canarios como yo. Y Lamine Yamal, obviamente", reconoció. Dos espejos en los que mirarse por aquello de compartir origen y un tercero que ha cambiado la percepción de lo que un adolescente es capaz de hacer sobre un terreno de juego. Cuando atendió a MARCA tras su exhibición ante Fiyi, todavía no había tenido tiempo de hablar con sus padres. Tenía el MVP entre las manos y una dedicatoria pendiente. "A ellos, a mi hermano, que los quiero mucho y son los mejores". La conversación terminó con una pregunta mucho más terrenal que cualquiera de las cifras que había dejado su actuación. ¿Dónde iba a guardar el trofeo? "En mi cuarto".

articles.title: Arsenal vs Dortmund: Champions League – Predictions, how to watch, lineups
articles.summary: Europe’s premier club competition pits English champions Arsenal against German league leaders Dortmund on Tuesday.
articles.body:
Who : Arsenal vs Borussia Dortmund What : UEFA Champions League Where : Emirates Stadium, London, United Kingdom When : Tuesday, November 24 at 8pm (20:00 GMT). How to follow : Al Jazeera Sport will bring you all the build-up from 17:00 GMT before our live text commentary stream.

Premier League holders Arsenal face German giants Borussia Dortmund for the first time in more than a decade, as the Champions League returns for matchday five action.

Arsenal and their fans were left frustrated at the weekend despite opening up a six-point lead at the top of the Premier League with a 2-2 draw at Newcastle United.

But a firm grip on their English top-flight title defence and a 10-game unbeaten streak across all competitions give Mikel Arteta’s side plenty of reasons to be optimistic for Tuesday’s UCL fixture in north London.

Dortmund, too, have been impressive in their own ways. Unbeaten in Germany this season, they sit two points clear of defending champions Bayern Munich atop the Bundesliga table. Niko Kovac’s team are also on an eight-match unbeaten run.

Eberechi Eze, who also scored in the last game, has been Arsenal’s leading scorer in this year’s Champions League with two goals so far, while fellow stars Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Martin Odegaard have also bagged a goal each.

In the Dortmund camp, veteran striker Serhou Guirassy is the outright leader with four goals – figures that also make him the joint fourth-highest in the competition.

How have Arsenal played in the Champions League?

Arsenal are third in the league phase standings, with 10 points from four games. The Gunners have won three games – against Napoli, Lille and Slavia Prague – and drawn once, with Bayern.

Only Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid have performed better than Arsenal, with 100 percent records.

How have Dortmund played in the Champions League?

Dortmund are 12th in the standings with nine points. They have won three games – against Villarreal, Sabah and Real Betis – and lost once, to Bodo/Glimt.

What happened the last time Arsenal and Dortmund met?

The last time the two teams met in a competitive match was in the 2014-15 season.

Dortmund won 2-0 in Germany in their first encounter and Arsenal beat them by the same scoreline in England in the reverse leg.

Opta’s supercomputer has picked Arsenal as favourites.

They are predicted to have a 65.2 percent chance of winning, while Dortmund’s odds of victory are 15.8 percent. A draw is a 19 percent probability.

(Last five matches across all competitions; latest game first)

Goalkeeper David Raya is doubtful after he was forced off in the second half against Newcastle with a shoulder injury and missed Monday’s training session.

Winger Saka has been sidelined for another month with a thigh injury and midfielder Martin Zubimendi, who picked up a hamstring injury on international duty, is out for a few weeks.

Kepa Arrizabalaga; Jurrien Timber, Ezri Konsa, Gabriel, Riccardo Calafiori; Bruno Guimaraes, Declan Rice; Noni Madueke, Martin Odegaard, Eberechi Eze; Kai Havertz

Dortmund have a long list of injured players, including Carney Chukwuemeka (muscle) and Emre Can (ACL).

Gregor Kobel; Waldemar Anton, Nico Schlotterbeck, Ramy Bensebaini; Julian Ryerson, Joey Veerman, Felix Nmecha, Daniel Svensson; Jobe Bellingham, Fabio Silva; Serhou Guirassy

United Kingdom: TNT Sports, Amazon Prime

You can find your regional broadcaster on UEFA’s official broadcaster listing .

articles.title: Fifa presidential race: Gianni Infantino private-jet flights under scrutiny
articles.summary: Fifa president Gianni Infantino's globetrotting by private jet since his plan to sell off a stake in the World Cup has come under scrutiny.
articles.body:
Fifa president Gianni Infantino's globetrotting by private jet since his plan to sell off a stake in the World Cup can be revealed.

BBC Sport found Infantino has taken 39 private flights - the equivalent of one every three days - and visited 32 different countries since the news emerged on 28 July.

Our research found he travelled more than 102,800 air miles and spent just under nine days in the air in the space of 115 days.

Critics have accused of Infantino of using tools only at his disposal as president to aid his campaign for re-election next March.

They questioned whether his re-election campaign may have partly motivated any promises made or support offered during those visits.

Fifa said Infantino had a "statutory duty to maintain and develop good relations between and among Fifa, the confederations, 211 member associations, political bodies, and international organisations".

However, he visited nearly double the 18 countries he did in the same period in 2025.

The initial Times story that revealed Infantino's World Cup plan led to a wave of criticism around the world.

But, as BBC Sport revealed, many observers feel Infantino is now the favourite to be re-elected in the spring after his rivals struggled to find a candidate to run against him until the last moment.

And it appears Infantino has managed to shore up support around the world, with critics suggesting his globetrotting was a key part of that strategy.

There has also been concern about the environmental impact of his extensive travels.

Miguel Maduro - a former head of Fifa's governance committee - said Infantino's travelling was "part of his campaign".

He told BBC Sport: "The issue here is that Fifa does not have rules on campaign funding, so the president can claim that he's going there on official business when indirectly he's using that to campaign.

"And anyone else running against him very likely will not have the financial means to compete with that."

Infantino's position seemed vulnerable after it emerged he had been devising a plan to sell stakes in the World Cup and other competitions to private investors, in a proposal called Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE).

Before FFE was abandoned, Infantino wrote to all 211 member associations saying they would receive $40m (£30m) if they backed the plan.

Lars-Christer Olsson - a former chief executive of Uefa - told BBC Sport the "important" question was "what does he promise and what are the conditions, as he already did when he promised cash if the members supported his FFE project?"

BBC Sport gleaned the information about where Infantino had been travelling to, and when, from postings on his social media accounts.

The reasons for his travels include holding meetings with football association presidents, opening pitches, meeting politicians and attending confederation gatherings.

The private jets he used are operated by Qatar Executive (QE) - a subsidiary of the Qatar Airways Group, which is one of Fifa's sponsors.

BBC Sport used flight-tracking records and the jet registrations of the Qatar Executive fleet to compile a detailed log of Infantino's flights, totalling at least 39 since the start of August. Fifa did not dispute the figure.

It said "all travel is in line with Fifa's regulations" and there are "rules which establish the framework for flights and travel by any Fifa official".

But Fifa declined to comment on how the use of QE flights impacts on the money available from the Qatar Airways sponsorship for the benefit of global football.

The governing body also declined to comment when asked when Infantino had last taken a commercial flight.

Olsson said: "What do these trips cost and who is paying, which are the implications for the total football community?

"Is he provided with transport in his private campaign with the idea of getting something back in return if he is elected? If Fifa is paying for private jets, would it not be better to invest this money in the member associations?"

Maduro said: "That's again a confusion between his role as president of Fifa and his role as candidate to Fifa presidency."

He said there were no regulations within Fifa on the "use of public money to support their campaign".

"There's no independent authority that controls that, there is no regulation of campaign funding," he said.

Infantino's trips included attending the Caribbean Football Union presidents' meeting and a junior football tournament in the Dominican Republic three weeks after FFE failed.

He then flew to Paris, where he attended the esports World Cup , alongside French President Emmanuel Macron and Saudi Arabia's Crown Prince Mohammed Bin Salman.

On his Instagram account, Infantino said he had "pledged Fifa's support" for the Pakistan Football Federation president's development plans when he met him in the US in September.

A few days later, he referenced a "wonderful discussion" with the president of the Latvian Football Federation during a visit to Riga, describing him as "my dear friend".

During a visit to Indonesia in October for the final of the Fifa ASEAN Cup, he met presidents from the football federations of Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Brunei Darussalam, Cambodia, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Malaysia, Maldives, Mongolia, Myanmar, Pakistan, Philippines, Qatar, Singapore, Thailand and Timor-Leste.

He said: "Having your support and shared passion on this momentous occasion means a great deal and together we will continue driving this game forward."

And during a recent trip to Manila, he performed on stage as part of a quartet called the 'Backache Boys', alongside officials from the Asian Football Confederation, and the football federations of Malaysia and the Philippines.

Based on our log of Infantino's private-jet flights, we calculated he spent 213 hours and 49 minutes in the air, travelling about 102,870 air miles.

For the type of private jet Infantino was using, this would produce an estimated 1,673 tonnes of CO2e emissions.

That's equivalent to the emissions 252 people would accumulate on average in an entire year, according to European Union data , external . These figures are conservative estimates based on average fuel burn rates.

Fifa has also been criticised for expanding the number of teams at World Cups, and hosting them in multiple countries, thereby increasing the amount of travel. The 2026 World Cup was described as the 'most polluting World Cup ever'.

Freddie Daley, from the Cool Down Sport for Climate Action Network, said Infantino's behaviour was "emblematic of Fifa's approach to environmental sustainability under his leadership: total and utter disregard".

"Despite numerous pledges, Fifa has failed to deliver any significant plan on how it will achieve them and has instead gone backwards," he added.

Maduro said Fifa's support for initiatives on climate action - which included being a signatory of the United Nation's Sports for Climate Action Framework - was "window dressing".

Fifa did not directly respond to a question about its justification for the environmental impact caused by Infantino's extensive travelling.

A spokesperson for Fifa said its objectives were to "improve football constantly and promote it globally".

They added: "The Fifa president has a statutory duty to maintain and develop good relations between and among Fifa, the confederations, 211 member associations, political bodies, and international organisations.

"To do that, he travels around the world and attends Fifa's tournaments and events. Mr Infantino is elected until 18 March 2027, when the next Fifa presidential election will take place.

"Fifa has put in place rules which establish the framework for flights and travel by any Fifa official.

"The Fifa president routinely travels around the world for various duties, together with relevant officials, on business and tournament-related matters and strives to visit member associations of Fifa whenever he can.

"Fifa expenses are published in our annual report, and all travel is in line with Fifa's regulations.

"Fifa's money belongs to the 211 member associations and an increased investment to $6.35bn for the upcoming cycle reinforces our unwavering commitment to further supporting football development and access globally."

articles.title: Vinicius y el enfoque correcto
articles.standfirst: El brasileño sigue la senda de Espí para ser útil al equipo mientras alcanza su punto óptimo
articles.summary: El brasileño sigue la senda de Espí para ser útil al equipo mientras alcanza su punto óptimo
articles.body: No va a ser fácil. Ni rápido. Pero Vinicius anda a la búsqueda del camino de baldosas amarillas para volver a Oz. El brasileño lleva muchos meses de infelicidad en el Santiago Bernabéu. Demasiados. Y mientras recupera la sonrisa y el baile, ofrece destellos de recuperación en un papel cada día más determinante, el de revulsivo. La visita del PSV Eindhoven, pesadilla del madridismo veterano, le concederá de nuevo galones de titular. Mourinho es zorro al gestionar una situación compleja. No es fácil reconectar a una estrella apagada. El caso es que, por primera vez, el portugués eligió ante el Celta, a Diomande, pero garantizó a Vini la foto inicial en Champions, que brilla más, mientras le enviaba al césped para activar la remontada. Y el chico cumplió. Con creces. Ya asomó esa versión eléctrica de Junior ante el Villarreal, pero su estupenda irrupción se fue por el sumidero con el ya famoso tirón de pelos y, sobre todo, las protestas posteriores. Fue participativo, eléctrico, persistente, con el foco puesto en el objetivo prioritario, ganar el partido, por encima que quién lo hiciese o en qué circunstancias. Fue precisamente lo que se apreció ante el Celta, un cambio perceptible en su juego. Alternó. Tuvo variedad. Y demostró que, además de un excelente regateador y rematador, sabe asociarse y ser asistente. Suya fue la diagonal interior para servir a Mbappé (con lo que les cuesta encontrarse) que activó el empate de Bellingham. Y suya fue la atracción a la defensa para poner el caramelo en la cabeza de Espí, el mejor ejemplo de cómo aprovechar cada minuto en el verde. El ariete suma sin levantar la voz, un enfoque imbatible que servirá a Vinicius para recuperar el fútbol mientras regresan la confianza y el tono físico perdidos, según confesión propia. Aseguró Florentino en la Asamblea que no dejará que el caso Negreira quede en nada. Tiene por delante una de las misiones más difíciles de sus dos mandatos.

articles.title: Wolves hit their stride, Stoke continue to dream but can they last the course and are QPR dark horses of Championship?
articles.summary: Wolves are improving defensively, Stoke look strong and QPR look resolute; Andy Hinchcliffe picks out the key stories in The Championship catch-up; a Sky Sports column focusing on the second tier.
articles.body:
Welcome to The Championship Catch-up, a new Sky Sports column in which Andy Hinchcliffe rounds up some of the key stories from the second tier. This week:

Wolves are coming together under Peixoto

Stoke look like they can last the course

Wolves have added solidity at the back to attacking prowess

With the players Wolves have got and the way they play, they were always going to score goals. They've averaged around 1.7 goals per game across those periods, so they're still good for a goal under Cesar Peixoto.

But in the last seven games they've conceded only five, compared to the 14 goals they shipped in their first nine. They're not playing defensively, they're just defending well. They're keeping the ball and keeping teams away from their penalty area.

At the start of the season they were too open. They were great to watch and scoring goals, but conceding too many. They needed to find a balance. They didn't have to become ultra-defensive, but they did need some defensive strength.

They've got plenty of attacking threats. Raul Jimenez is still missing, but Adam Armstrong is doing really well and is a proven goalscorer at this level. They've got width, dynamism and options, while Andre plays a really important role sitting deep in midfield.

All I was looking for was more balanced performances. They didn't need to let the goals dry up just to keep clean sheets. They've managed to find that balance and do both. They're dominating games, keeping teams out and still scoring goals.

Even when they change the right-back, centre-half or left-back, they can maintain that defensive strength. They're clearly moving in the right direction and are now a much more balanced, complete team.

Kieran Trippier's experience has been invaluable. He cares about the club getting promoted back to the Premier League. Individually, he wants to do well, but he also wants the team to succeed.

He's perhaps not the player he was five years ago, but he can still have a huge effect. He'll have to get used to the fact that he might not play every game, but Wolves have the depth to manage that.

With Trippier, it's not just about his ability but also his leadership and experience. He can reinforce the standards they should be setting and what they're looking to achieve this season.

Can Stoke City last the course under Mark Robins?

Stoke City have won 10 of 16 games, more than any other Championship team. Would you have expected them to have won more games than Wolves, West Ham, Middlesbrough or Southampton after 16 matches? Probably not.

They're still overachieving in terms of the data, but Mark Robins spoke during the international break about the need to improve their performances. The league position doesn't really tell you how good you are. You have to monitor performances and look at how to develop and improve.

There's still work to do at both ends of the pitch, but they're getting goals from different players. George Hirst came in for big money and had been struggling for goals and not starting games. He won them the game against Birmingham, which is a lift for him and the team.

Against Birmingham, they were down to 10 men for a long time and showed the resilience to hold on to a 1-0 lead. When you look at everything, the foundations are there for them to get better.

How many experienced, very good coaches have gone to Stoke and not been able to make it work? We all hoped Mark Robins would succeed because of the work he did at Coventry, but there was always the question of whether he would become another coach who fell foul of a club where nobody seemed able to get things going.

I just think it's wonderful that it's him because he's such a brilliant coach. He's very understated and humble. I saw him after a game recently and asked him a couple of tactical questions. He was saying he was glad I'd noticed certain things he'd done. He's very engaging, but it's not all about him. It's about the job he's there to do.

Player for player, this Stoke side is better than last season's team. That's what I'm saying about their recruitment and the shape Mark is playing. They're better, and the fact they can improve further makes things look really positive.

But we're only 16 games into a long season. Mark will know winter is really tough for every team, particularly when you're up near the top and everyone is looking to knock you off your position. They'll be looking at their performances and adjusting their training because that's all you can do.

Could Stoke possibly be in the mix for a top-two finish? With the way they're playing and the players they've got, who could improve further, very possibly.

QPR have shown defensive improvements this season

Defensively for QPR there's been the big shift this season. They were 23rd last season for goals conceded and are now in the top four. That's the foundation. If you don't concede too many goals in the Championship, you've got a chance.

I don't think they're a defensive team. They're a team that defend well. It doesn't mean they're sitting everybody behind the ball and playing on the counter-attack. They can dominate possession and force opponents backwards. They defend well, but they're not defensive.

Jimmy Dunne, Ronnie Edwards and Pierce Charles are absolutely crucial, but the team structure is there too. They've got a solid base and the nice problem now is working out how to be more creative.

It was important to win at Millwall and maintain their momentum in the top eight, but they won't always find themselves in such a dominant position. There's still work to do going forward to become more threatening and dangerous.

They need to find a regular goalscorer, but they also need to create more chances. Getting Ilias Chair back into the team regularly is important. He's one of those players who can affect games in the Championship.

This has to be a big season for Chair. He undoubtedly has the ability, but at times he's coasted along and hasn't become the dominant force Rangers need him to be.

If they want to improve going forward and finish in the top eight, he's key. He's got the movement, intelligence and creative quality, and he can score goals. It's not just about what he can do himself, but what he can do for the players around him.

Looking at his performance against Millwall and what he could bring for the rest of the season, I think he's key to improving their attack. It's down to him to drive that improvement.

articles.summary: El conjunto blanco recibe al PSV Eindhoven este martes en el Santiago Bernabéu en la quinta jornada de la fase de liga

articles.title: La Real, ante una de sus etapas reinas
articles.standfirst: El conjunto txuriurdin disputará cuatro partidos en sólo 10 días, con su futuro europeo en juego y puntos muy valiosos en LaLiga ante Sevilla, Real Madrid y Villarreal
articles.summary: El conjunto txuriurdin disputará cuatro partidos en sólo 10 días, con su futuro europeo en juego y puntos muy valiosos en LaLiga ante Sevilla, Real Madrid y Villarreal
articles.body: La Real Sociedad afrontará desde este jueves una de las etapas reinas de su cargada temporada por la presencia en cuatro competiciones, ya que va a disputar cuatro partidos en solamente 10 días, jugándose las últimas opciones de estar en el top 8 de la Europa League y puntos muy valiosos en LaLiga ante rivales de la entidad de Sevilla, Real Madrid y Villarreal. ¡Casi nada! La Real, para empezar, visitará este jueves al Crystal Palace en Londres con la obligación de obtener la victoria, si quiere seguir pensando que puede concluir la fase Liga entre los ocho primeros clasificados y librarse de la ronda de dieciseisavos. Con una única victoria hasta la fecha parece complicado, pero la igualdad que hay dan aún opciones a los de Matarazzo si vencen en esta cita. Después de conocer si puede cumplir o ya no el que era su primer objetivo europeo, el conjunto txuriurdin recibirá en Anoeta al Sevilla, el equipo que justo le sigue en la clasificación, por lo que serán tres puntos muy valiosos ante uno de sus rivales por los puestos europeos. La Real tendrá sólo 68 horas para recuperarse del cansancio y medirse nada más y nada menos que al Real Madrid el miércoles ya 2 de diciembre, aunque al menos lo hará de nuevo de local. De nuevo apenas tres días más tarde, tendrá que jugar a domicilio con el Villarreal, décimo clasificado y otro de los equipos que quieren acabar en la zona continental. Pellegrino Matarazzo y sus futbolistas no paran de tener fases complicadas de calendario, pero estos próximos 10 días van a ser una de las que más por lo que se juega en Europa y por la entidad de los rivales en LaLiga. Sin duda alguna, una de las etapas más duras de esta larga campaña llena de partidos para soñar con objetivos ambiciosos.

articles.title: Pablo Villa alerta a Mourinho: "El ruido de lo que dice puede eclipsar lo que pasa en el campo"
articles.standfirst: El periodista analizó en 'La Tribu' del impacto del entrenador portugués en el Real Madrid, aunque cuestiona sus últimas salidas de tono ante los medios
articles.summary: El periodista analizó en 'La Tribu' del impacto del entrenador portugués en el Real Madrid, aunque cuestiona sus últimas salidas de tono ante los medios
articles.body: José Mourinho ha conseguido convencer al vestuario del Real Madrid y los resultados empiezan a respaldar su trabajo. Sin embargo, no todo son elogios para el técnico portugués. Pablo Villa analizó en 'La Tribu' de Radio MARCA las dos caras del entrenador: su notable rendimiento deportivo y su comportamiento ante los micrófonos, que empieza a generar demasiado ruido. "Ha caído de pie en el vestuario del Real Madrid y no lo tenía fácil", comenzó explicando. Villa recordó las dificultades que afrontaba Mourinho después de dos años de sequía y destacó su capacidad para corregir algunos de los problemas que arrastraba el equipo. Las nueve victorias consecutivas son, a su juicio, un argumento incontestable para valorar su trabajo. El periodista puso especialmente en valor la recuperación de varios futbolistas. Bellingham, Valverde, Vinicius y Arda Güler han dado pasos adelante con el portugués, mientras que también destacó el rendimiento de Bernardo Silva. "Deportivamente, poco que reprochar y mucho que reconocer", sentenció. Sin embargo, Villa separó el rendimiento deportivo de la actitud de Mourinho ante los medios de comunicación. El periodista considera que el entrenador ha recuperado comportamientos que ya forman parte de su trayectoria y que pueden terminar perjudicando su propia imagen. Las fotografías que llevó a la sala de prensa tras el derbi, el plantón a los periodistas después del encuentro ante el Villarreal y sus declaraciones sobre Santi Comesaña fueron algunos de los ejemplos que puso sobre la mesa. Villa también se refirió a la polémica arbitral y a las diferencias de criterio a la hora de amonestar a los futbolistas del Real Madrid y del Barcelona. No obstante, lanzó una advertencia sobre la utilización constante del caso Negreira: "Ver los fantasmas de Negreira por sistema puede acabar nublando la mirada incluso de quienes tienen motivos para desconfiar". Su conclusión fue clara: Mourinho tiene argumentos futbolísticos suficientes para defender su trabajo y no necesita alimentar polémicas fuera del terreno de juego. "Sería una pena que el ruido de sus ruedas de prensa terminase por eclipsar lo mucho y bien que está haciendo sobre el césped", concluyó.

articles.title: La doble M del Leganés empieza a meter miedo
articles.standfirst: Álex Millán y Álvaro Morata lideran el resurgir goleador del conjunto pepinero desde la llegada de Luis Carrión
articles.summary: Álex Millán y Álvaro Morata lideran el resurgir goleador del conjunto pepinero desde la llegada de Luis Carrión
articles.body: El Leganés parece haber encontrado su pareja de baile en ataque. Álex Millán y Álvaro Morata, la doble M del conjunto pepinero, empiezan a demostrar todo su potencial y se han convertido en dos de los grandes protagonistas de la mejoría del equipo desde la llegada de Luis Carrión al banquillo. Los dos delanteros atraviesan un gran momento de forma y sus goles empiezan a traducirse en victorias para los blanquiazules. Especialmente significativo está siendo el despertar goleador de Álvaro Morata. Después de varios meses sin ver portería, al internacional español se le empiezan a caer los goles. Cuatro tantos en las últimas cuatro jornadas de Liga, con un doblete ante el Valladolid y sendas dianas frente al Albacete y al Andorra. Por su parte, Álex Millán acumula cinco goles en sus últimos seis compromisos oficiales, viendo portería de manera consecutiva ante el Trival Valderas, el Burgos y el Andorra. Ambos suman cuatro tantos en Liga, cinco en el caso del aragonés contando la Copa. Y, de mantener esta dinámica, tienen argumentos para alcanzar los dobles dígitos goleadores esta temporada. Además, empiezan a entenderse sobre el terreno de juego, como quedó demostrado en Andorra, donde Morata asistió a Millán en el tanto del empate antes de firmar él mismo el segundo gol pepinero. Algo está cambiando en este Leganés. La apuesta del técnico catalán por jugar con dos delanteros y recuperar el protagonismo de los hombres de banda está dando sus frutos. Futbolistas como Álex Sancris también están adquiriendo un mayor peso en el juego ofensivo de un equipo que ha logrado marcar seis goles en sus dos últimas jornadas. Las victorias ante el Burgos y el Andorra han devuelto la sonrisa a un vestuario que llevaba demasiadas semanas sin motivos para celebrar. Ahora, el objetivo es dar continuidad a esas buenas sensaciones, aunque habrá que estar pendientes de la evolución de Morata, que se retiró con molestias del encuentro en tierras andorranas. Precisamente, otra M se ha cruzado en el camino del Leganés. El Mirandés será el próximo rival de los pepineros en la Copa del Rey, en una eliminatoria que se disputará el miércoles 2 de diciembre a las 20.00 horas en Anduva y que estará cargada de morbo. Todavía está muy reciente lo sucedido en la última jornada de la pasada temporada, cuando un gol precisamente de Álex Millán certificó la permanencia del Leganés en Segunda y condenó al conjunto jabato al descenso a Primera Federación. Un encuentro marcado también por la polémica arbitral, con dos goles anulados al Mirandés. Ganas de revancha y de prolongar el buen momento por parte de los pepineros. Antes, este viernes, espera el Sabadell en Butarque. Los de Luis Carrión buscarán encadenar su tercera victoria consecutiva en Liga, alejarse de los problemas clasificatorios y empezar a mirar hacia arriba. Todavía queda mucha temporada y, con la doble M enchufada, el Leganés tiene motivos para volver a ilusionarse.

articles.title: Hugo Sánchez: "Aquel 0-0 ante el PSV fue triste, esa Copa de Europa era 'nuestra'"
articles.standfirst: El mexicano recuerda para MARCA la semifinal de la Copa de Europa 1988 ante el rival de hoy
articles.summary: El mexicano recuerda para MARCA la semifinal de la Copa de Europa 1988 ante el rival de hoy
articles.body: Habla Hugo Sánchez, mito del Real Madrid. Lo hace desde Cancún (México), a punto de montarse en un avión para Ciudad de México, donde trabaja para la ESPN. Sus recuerdos de aquella semifinal entre PSV y RM en 1988 son claros y amargos: “Si, estoy de acuerdo con que fue el momento más cercano que tuvimos en esa época para llegar a la final de la Copa de Europa. Eran otros tiempos, con sorteos muy complicados y una Copa en la que sólo jugaban los campeones de cada país. La dificultad era mayor, creo, y, a veces, era muy injusta todo pues por el sorteo te podía tocar la vuelta de visitante, con lo que suponía entonces esos campos de Europa”. La amargura de Hugo viene también por el rival, que no era uno de los grandes de Europa, aunque luego se proclamara campeón del continente: “El recuerdo es poco agradable, pues estuvimos muy cerca de pasar y ganar contra una rival, como el PSV, que no era de los más complicados. Quiero decir, que no era un Bayern, como nos tocó en la temporada anterior, la 86-87 en esa misma instancia de semifinales”. “Éramos los favoritos. Se nos escapó el triunfo ya en casa (1-1). El gol de penalti lo anoté yo... y con 1-0, y a falta de pocos minutos, nos empataron en el Bernabéu. Ese empate nos debilitó por el valor doble del gol de visitante en el partido en Holanda”, nos recuerda Hugo, que fue titular en los dos partidos. Aquel Real Madrid de la Quinta del Buitre y la Quinta de los Machos, como el mismo Hugo nos recuerda, ganó cinco Ligas, pero.... “Nos dolió mucho lo de ese día de Eindhoven, porque, con las cinco Ligas seguidas que ganamos, era un momento oportuno para ganar esa Copa de Europa”. “En la vuelta tuvimos varias ocasiones. Ellos iban a por el 0-0 y así jugaron, a la defensiva, y nosotros, por contra, con agresividad. Butragueño tuvo una al inicio, y no acertamos. También recuerdo la ‘chilena’ que hice a falta de cinco minutos y tampoco entró. El héroe fue el portero de ellos, Van Breukelen, y me paró aquel remate tan especial para mí. A partir de ese partido se convirtió en héroe nacional de Holanda”. La convicción de Hugo es enorme: “Si hubiéramos llegado a la final, estoy seguro de que la íbamos a ganar y hasta sin problemas [fue ante el Benfica]. De hecho, el PSV la ganó. Como le pasó al Bayern (finalista), al Steaua, antes, y al Milan en la 88-89. Fuimos la motivación y el trampolín para los rivales. Por eso, tenemos el sabor amargo de no conseguir ninguna y la del PSV fue la que estuvo más cerca. Era la gran oportunidad de conquistar la nuestra. Y digo más: en esos cinco años de títulos de Liga, con las reglas de ahora en la Champions, hubiéramos ganado por lo menos tres de las cinco Copas de Europa”. La reflexión final de Hugo es diáfana: “Se nos escapó esa gran oportunidad de quedar en la historia. Nos faltó ese título para redondear esa, por entonces, segunda época dorada del Real Madrid tras la de Di Stéfano. Ganamos cinco Ligas, dos UEFA (yo sólo una), y pudimos dejar el sello de la Copa de Europa, pero fue triste no hacerlo”. ¿Qué pasó en vestuarios tras el choque de Eindhoven? "Fueron momentos difíciles -dice HS-. El árbitro no fue cómplice de ellos, pero no nos dio más minutos extra, por lo menos los cinco que se merecían. No dio casi nada de descuento y tenía prisa de irse con el 0-0. Míchel, Buyo y yo fuimos a reclamarle y creo que a Míchel le expulsaron, y luego le metieron dos o tres partidos pues nuestra protesta fue fuerte. Había mucho enfado y decepción en el vestuario. Una tristeza grande, pues ganar esa Copa de Europa fue lo único que nos faltó en esa generación".

images.caption: Hugo conduce la pelota aquel día. LUIS GABRIEL

articles.title: Deschamps tiene nuevo equipo: ficha como jefe de cocina por un dineral
articles.summary: Didier Deschamps, exseleccionador de Francia, ha protagonizado un regreso bastante inesperado al primer plano al protagonizar una campaña navideña de 'Burger King'.
articles.body: Didier Deschamps, exseleccionador de Francia, ha protagonizado un regreso bastante inesperado al primer plano al protagonizar una campaña navideña de 'Burger King'. En el anuncio el antiguo seleccionador de 'Les Bleus' se pone al frente de una brigada de cocina para preparar hamburguesas de la marca estadounidense. "Creo que Deschamps se dio cuenta de que, en el fondo, esto le venía bien a su imagen. Cuando le mostramos el anuncio terminado, nos dio las gracias. Porque es consciente de que también le beneficia a él; muestra una faceta suya muy simpática... ¿Cuánto le hemos pagado? Cuesta lo que vale su popularidad. Estamos hablando, más bien, de cientos de miles de euros", explicó el director de la agencia en RMC Sport. "Tuvo que comprometerse a no firmar con ningún club ni federación antes de la emisión del anuncio. ¡Porque tenía que "fichar" por Burger King!", desveló Julien Levilain, director de la agencia Buzzman. El anuncio de Didier Deschamps para Burger King, que dura un minuto y quince segundos, sólo se ha emitido una vez en televisión hasta el momento: el sábado por la noche, durante el descanso del partido de rugby entre Francia y Argentina.

articles.title: Major League Soccer: FC Cincinnati to honour city zoo's deceased hippo Fiona
articles.summary: Major League Soccer side FC Cincinnati will honour Fiona, a hippo that recently died at the city's zoo, with a tifo display at their match with Nashville SC on Saturday.
articles.body:
Major League Soccer side FC Cincinnati will honour Fiona, a hippo that recently died at the city's zoo, with a tifo display at their match with Nashville SC on Saturday.

Fiona, a social media star since her premature birth at the zoo in 2017, died on Thursday after swallowing a woollen hat that had slipped into her enclosure.

The Ohio side will now raise a banner depicting the nine-year-old semi-aquatic mammal in their post-season MLS Cup encounter with Nashville, who won the Supporters' Shield for being the highest-placed team in the league campaign.

Cincinnati said Fiona was a "beloved hippo who became a symbol of Cincinnati and captured hearts around the world".

The tifo will be produced by fan group The Forge Cincy, who painted the display on Sunday in a garage next to Cincinnati's TQL Stadium.

The club will also make a donation in Fiona's memory for every fan in attendance to the Cincinnati Zoo and Botanical Garden.

Removal of hat inside Fiona the hippo was 'impossible', Cincinnati Zoo says

Fiona the hippo dies after swallowing a hat at Cincinnati Zoo

Cincinnati's Nick Hagglund, who hails from the city and is in his eighth season with the team, previously paid tribute to Fiona after scoring in his side's 3-1 victory over Orlando on the day of her death.

The defender yelled "that's for Fiona", mimicking the ears on top of her head, in a celebration video , external on the club's Instagram.

Later, on his Instagram account , external , Hagglund posted, "This one was for her @fionahippo @cincinnatizoo.

"Cincinnati needed a win on the day after the passing of our beloved hippo, a symbol of hope and resilience for our city, and the lads answered the call."

Cincinnati's tifo is one of a number of tributes paid to the hippo, with Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Tee Higgins wearing a Fiona sweater , external prior to his American football franchise's defeat by the Washington Commanders on Monday.

Meanwhile handlers of the blue hippo balloon at New York's annual Macy's Thanksgiving Parade will wear a purple patch in her honour.

At birth, Fiona weighed 13kg (29lb), which the zoo said was about half the previous lowest recorded birth weight for her species, and she previously inspired an ice cream flavour and a character in Cincinnati's ballet.

Fiona swallowed the woollen hat around 10 days prior to her death, with the item getting into her enclosure by accident after a visitor tossed it in the air and it caught on a ceiling fan that flung it through a small opening.

"We probably couldn't make [it] happen again if we tried," said zoo spokesperson Michelle Curley.

Hippos normally live up to 50 years in human care, according to the zoo.

Nashville finished top of the MLS Eastern Conference, 31 points ahead of ninth-placed Cincinnati.

However, having beaten Orlando in a one-off wildcard round, Cincinnati defeated Nashville 1-0 in the opening match of their best-of-three round one series.

Should Cincinnati win on Saturday they will progress to a one-off conference semi-final with either Chicago Fire or Charlotte FC, with a conference final prior to the season-ending MLS Cup final.

articles.title: Birmingham City, Stoke City, West Bromwich Albion and Wolves in the Championship top five - can it last?
articles.summary: With more than a third of the season gone, Stoke City, Birmingham City, Wolves and West Brom are all in the Championship promotion race. Who can keep it up?
articles.body:
It is beginning to look a lot like Christmas for followers of Midlands football.

Granted, it is actually only November, but with more than a third of the 2026-27 Championship season gone, already the table is taking on an increasingly familiar weekly look in terms of the primary promotion contenders.

There has been many a year when there have been early-season stirrings in the Midlands, only for the momentum to fade.

But Coventry City proved it can be done after 25 years away from the Premier League. And now Stoke City, Wolves, Birmingham City and West Bromwich Albion are all in contention to join both the Sky Blues and Aston Villa in the top flight.

Stoke in second, Wolves third, Blues fourth and Albion fifth makes for both a heartening, yet surprising sight, with only Middlesbrough in front of them.

It is only six months since Wolves were relegated and, for all the summer discontent at Molineux and doubts among disillusioned fans about their worthiness as serious candidates, the fact is they are very much in the mix.

But, while most people at Molineux can now at least contemplate a quick return, for their local rivals the parachute payments have long since expired.

Blues have been away the longest, their 15-year absence from the top flight having even included a one-season return to the third tier and back.

But, given their extensive American backing, the club have ambitions to be serious contenders - and the only surprise was that it took so long to find their feet.

For Stoke and Albion to be up there was not necessarily forecast, but it has made for all the more happy motoring for the BBC correspondents who cover the quartet of clubs on a regular basis.

BBC Sport asked reporters from BBC Stoke & Staffordshire and BBC West Midlands Sport for their analysis of the season so far and what lies in store for each club...

Next five fixtures: Millwall (H), West Ham (A), QPR (H), Lincoln (A), West Brom (H)

Championship finishes since last in the Premier League: 16th, 15th, 14th, 14th, 16th, 17th, 18th, 17th

'A full-blown revolution over the past three months'

Mark Elliott, BBC Radio Stoke commentator

Mark Robins has spoken a lot about evolution and incremental gains in his time as Stoke City manager, but it's hard to escape the feeling that there's been a full-blown revolution over the past three months.

Stoke began the season with three defeats, a manager under pressure and the impending loss of their most productive player in Sorba Thomas - but a change in formation, an excellent summer transfer window and an unbelievable run of form has quietened all dissenting voices.

Thirty two out of a possible 39 points from 13 games since the window closed is a brilliant record - but Stoke are maybe still short of truly turning the hopefully optimistic among their fans into true believers.

Most of that is a hangover from last season's promising start eventually falling apart, but there are substantial differences.

The squad has more quality and depth, a more ambitious way of playing and the less quantifiable qualities of tenacity and resilience and a mental strength that, coupled with defensive solidity, has allowed them to find multiple ways to win close games.

Luke Graham, Ethan Galbraith, Jack McGlynn and Ben Johnson have been their most eye-catching summer acquisitions but several who struggled last season, Eric Bocat first among them, have found success too.

The next step is to create more chances and score more goals, whilst maintaining anything close to their current return of points per game.

Even the most hardened pessimists will then maybe see a play-off place as a realistic aim for 2027.

Stoke reached a different level - Robins

Next five fixtures: Derby (H), Lincoln (A), Southampton (H), QPR (A), Millwall (H)

Championship finishes since last in the Premier League: Relegated (2026)

By Mike Taylor, BBC Radio WM commentator

Only a point behind, and with the feeling they have not played to their full ability very often yet - not very often for 90 consecutive minutes, certainly - Wolves are not badly placed.

Their supporters can be hard taskmasters at the moment, and can hardly be blamed for that in view of the mess of recent seasons and the big promises made of going full-tilt to get straight back up.

For all the understandable misgivings, though, there is a clear path towards achieving it.

Reaching the end of that path may require some judicious spending in January to tidy up a squad that still looks imbalanced, with a surfeit of players in some areas and a shortage in others.

Personal surges in form, from Fer Lopez early in the season to Adam Armstrong more recently, have covered up the gaps and reminded everyone that this squad is not short of class at this level.

Cesar Peixoto, new to England, has handled a delicate situation in a tumultuous league with quiet confidence.

He will have to complete the job in May before he can claim credit more widely, but appears to realise the power he can harness if, like a certain Portuguese predecessor, he can unify all the forces around the club to point in the same direction.

Wolves' Mane of the moment has to now kick on

Next five fixtures: Burnley (A), Bolton (H), Charlton (A), Watford (H), Portsmouth (A)

Finishes since last in the Premier League: Fourth (lost to Blackpool in play-offs), 12th, 21st, 10th, 10th, 19th, 19th, 17th, 20th, 18th, 20th, 17th, 22nd, League One champions, 10th

For all of the outside noise about the future of Chris Davies, the Birmingham City board have steadfastly backed their man. Now that decision is paying dividends.

Thanks to that rarely tried footballing trait of continuity, they spent the international break sitting at the top of a very congested Championship table.

But Saturday's 1-0 loss against 10-man Stoke was a reminder of just how tight the division is.

The reboot of the squad started in earnest in January, when the future for Davies was at its wobbliest.

The £18m-plus combined investment in Colombian midfielder Jhon Solis, Danish striker August Priske and Spanish winger Carlos Vicente gave them a chance to bed in to English football over the second half of this season, before kicking on this time around.

Priske, at 22, has a high ceiling. His six Championship goals this season has come with improved physicality and increased confidence.

The industry and physique of Solis have stabilised Blues midfield, while Vicente is one of four options on the wing following the loan addition of Liam Millar.

Davies himself has learned from his first Championship season. His team are now versatile, more able to move the ball forward quickly, no longer wedded to possession at all costs.

Defensively too there is a greater resilience and a visible hunger to succeed.

Whether they are serious contenders for automatic promotion remains to be seen, but they have the ingredients to retain a top six spot over the full 46-game course."

Little solace - and no Solis - in setback at Stoke

Next five fixtures: Bolton (A), Bristol City (H), Portsmouth (A), Cardiff (H), Stoke (A)

Championship finishes since last in Premier League: 10th, ninth, fifth, ninth, 21st

'Wild to think the difference Morrison has made'

James Morrison's mind was at ease over this international break following Albion's 3-0 win over Millwall.

He is refusing to reveal any pre-season expectations, but looking at the Championship table makes for satisfying reading.

Certainly externally, nobody expected the Baggies to be fifth - just one point off the automatic promotion places - a third into this campaign.

Morrison has now racked up 51 points from 30 league games in charge. That includes his three interim spells, although the second was a single game as head coach in the FA Cup in January against their next opponents, Swansea City - in between the dismal reigns of Ryan Mason and Eric Ramsay.

It is wild to think of the difference Morrison and his excellent coaching staff have made in 2026.

Albion were heading in the direction of League One when the key were handed to the club legend, who'd been in the back seat the entire time.

A 10-game unbeaten run steered them to safety, and he even had to navigate a points deduction from the EFL for a breach of financial rules.

The club is in a much better place on and off the field, with Mozza now firmly at the wheel.

The upcoming January transfer window could play a big part in determining whether they continue on this positive path, but Baggies fans are at least enjoying the ride again.

articles.title: Republic of Ireland Women: Carla Ward signs contract extension
articles.summary: Republic of Ireland manager Carla Ward signs a contract extension until the conclusion of the side's Euro 2029 campaign.
articles.body:
Republic of Ireland manager Carla Ward has signed a contract extension until the conclusion of the side's Euro 2029 campaign.

The 42-year-old's previous deal was due to expire at the end of this World Cup qualification cycle but her future has now been resolved before next month's two-legged play-off final against Poland.

Ward replaced Eileen Gleeson at the helm in January 2025 and has led the side to promotion to League A in the Nations League and a highest ever position of 21st in the Fifa rankings.

The Republic of Ireland are just 180 minutes from next summer's World Cup in Brazil, with the first leg against Poland in Gdansk on 1 December before the reverse fixture four days later at Aviva Stadium.

"From the moment I arrived, I've felt a strong connection with this country, the players, the staff and, most importantly, the people. The way I've been welcomed and embraced has meant a huge amount to me, and it's a real privilege to lead this team and this nation," said Ward.

"I'm incredibly proud of what we've achieved together so far, but what excites me most is what lies ahead. There's something really special about this group, their togetherness, their character and their willingness to fight for each other and for the jersey.

"I've always said I want to build something that people can connect with, a team that reflects the spirit of this country, that people are proud of and genuinely feel part of. We've had some brilliant moments already, but I really believe we're only just getting started."

Two down, two to go - Irish target back-to-back World Cups

Mustaki out of World Cup play-off with knee injury

Contract extensions shows 'ambition to keep moving forward'

Ward previously managed Sheffield United, Aston Villa and Birmingham City after a successful playing career during which she scored over 100 goals for Sheffield FC.

Since she became boss, the Republic of Ireland have won 12 of their 19 games and lost just one of their Nations League fixtures last year with the sole reverse coming away to Slovenia.

Football Association of Ireland (FAI) chief executive officer David Courell said Ward has helped give "women and girls' football around the country the platform it deserves" during her tenure.

"We are delighted to reach agreement with Carla to continue to lead our Ireland women's national team for the long term," he added.

"The energy that she has brought to the role has propelled the team towards, hopefully, qualifying for a second Fifa Women's World Cup and, in turn, giving women and girls' football around the country the platform it deserves.

"Extending Carla's contract shows our ambition to keep moving forward, hopefully to the World Cup in Brazil and beyond to the Uefa European Championships in Germany in 2029."

The Republic of Ireland are aiming to secure a spot at their second successive World Cup, while Poland have never qualified for the tournament before.

Ward's side defeated Kazakhstan in comfortable fashion in their play-off semi-final with Poland coming through a penalty shootout against Belgium.

Republic of Ireland must do without key defender Chloe Mustaki who has been forced to withdraw from the panel after rupturing her anterior cruciate ligament (ACL).

articles.title: De fichaje estrella al ostracismo
articles.standfirst: Jon Morcillo ha pasado de llegar como uno de los grandes refuerzos del mercado invernal a jugar un papel residual en el Almería
articles.summary: Jon Morcillo ha pasado de llegar como uno de los grandes refuerzos del mercado invernal a jugar un papel residual en el Almería
articles.body: Hace menos de un año, el nombre de Jon Morcillo estaba entre los grandes protagonistas del mercado de invierno de Segunda división. El Almería decidió adelantarse a todos y desembolsó medio millón de euros al Albacete para incorporarlo antes de que finalizara su contrato. Era uno de los extremos más cotizados de la categoría, un futbolista diferencial llamado a dar un salto a Primera y una incorporación que despertó una enorme ilusión en el entorno rojiblanco. Hoy, apenas once meses después, su realidad es completamente distinta. El aterrizaje de Morcillo en el conjunto indálico fue inmejorable. Rubi le dio la alternativa como titular y el extremo respondió marcando en sus dos primeras titularidades, primero frente al Ceuta en casa y después en el Nuevo Mirandilla ante el Cádiz. Todo hacía indicar que el vasco estaba llamado a convertirse en una pieza fundamental para afrontar el tramo decisivo del campeonato. Sin embargo, la situación cambió de forma radical con el paso de las semanas. A partir de mediados de marzo comenzó a perder protagonismo hasta desaparecer prácticamente de las alineaciones. En los últimos 12 encuentros de la fase regular, únicamente fue titular en una ocasión, además de repetir en el partido de ida de las semifinales de playoffs frente al Castellón. Un frenazo inesperado para un jugador que había llegado con la etiqueta de refuerzo estrella. Lejos de revertirse con el cambio de entrenador, su escenario ha empeorado todavía más esta temporada. La llegada de García Pimienta no ha supuesto un nuevo comienzo para Morcillo, sino todo lo contrario. El extremo apenas ha participado en 6 de las 15 jornadas disputadas y su presencia frente al Ceuta se limitó a los cuatro minutos del tiempo añadido. De hecho, rompió una racha de cuatro encuentros consecutivos sin jugar un solo minuto. Su única titularidad del curso llegó en Sabadell. Desde entonces, el protagonismo del atacante ha ido disminuyendo hasta quedar relegado a un papel prácticamente testimonial en un Almería que, paradójicamente, atraviesa el mejor momento de la temporada y lidera la clasificación. Resulta difícil encontrar un caso de involución tan acusado en tan poco tiempo. Morcillo pasó de ser considerado uno de los mejores futbolistas de la categoría y uno de los fichajes más importantes del mercado invernal a quedar completamente fuera de la rotación. Un escenario que pocos podían imaginar cuando el Almería apostó fuerte por él y que convierte al extremo en uno de los grandes interrogantes de la plantilla rojiblanca. Porque el talento sigue estando ahí, pero su protagonismo se ha esfumado casi por completo.

articles.title: Jesús Owono ya se entrena en solitario con el Andorra
articles.standfirst: El guardameta realizó su primera aparición pública en el partido ante el Leganés y ha acudido a las instalaciones para trabajar tras el entrenamiento de la primera plantilla
articles.summary: El guardameta realizó su primera aparición pública en el partido ante el Leganés y ha acudido a las instalaciones para trabajar tras el entrenamiento de la primera plantilla
articles.body: Jesús Owono ya ha empezado el trabajo físico. Tras varias semanas centrado en la recuperación mental, aún queda mucho trabajo por delante, el portero del Andorra ha vuelto a entrenarse, eso sí en solitario, en las instalaciones del club. Después de realizar su primera aparición pública en el partido del viernes contra el Leganés. El guardameta, sancionado con 12 partidos, empezó a entrenarse la semana pasada en solitario y el lunes continuó con sus sesiones en solitario. Owono acudió a los campos de entrenamiento y tras la sesión grupal de sus compañeros ha realizado algunos ejercicios físicos, aún sin hacer portería y ponerse los guantes. Owono coincidió en el Estadi Comunal con los compañeros que no le han dejado sólo ni un instante. La plantilla se ha volcado con el portero desde el primer día y muchos de ellos le visitan casi a diario. De momento, el club del Principado no ha anunciado de manera oficial la vuelta del portero internacional por Guinea Ecuatorial. De hecho no hay fecha fijada y todo dependerá del estado mental del jugador que sigue con el tratamiento con especialistas para intentar superar la tragedia. La jugada entre Jesús Owono y Jesús de Miguel sucedió el 2 de noviembre en el tramo final del encuentro en el estadio Heliodoro Rodríguez López. El delantero madrileño sufrió un severo impacto en el pecho con la rodilla del portero del Andorra, con una parada cardiorrespiratorio. Al día siguiente, falleció en el hospital.

articles.title: Nuevo frenazo para Bajcetic
articles.standfirst: Tendrá que parar las próximas semanas por una lesión
articles.summary: Tendrá que parar las próximas semanas por una lesión
articles.body: Después de año y medio de baja por una sucesión de problemas físicos, Stefan Bajcetic se ve obligado a parar nuevamente por una lesión muscular, sufrida en el abductor de la pierna izquierda en el partido del pasado domingo ante el Valladolid. Desde su reaparición, el pasado 24 de octubre en Girona, el céltico había encadenado participación en 5 encuentros de Liga en los que sumó 99 minutos, siendo únicamente titular ante el Albacete, partido en el que disputó el primer tiempo. Su encuentro con más minutos. Este nuevo parón es un palo para un futbolista de gran talento cuya prometedora carrera se ha visto frenada las últimas temporadas por problemas físicos y que ha vuelto a Vigo con ganas de llegar a medio plazo al primer equipo céltico. Fredi Álvarez, técnico del Celta Fortuna, lamenta este nuevo obstáculo para el mediocampista: "Frena su adaptación a la competición. Estamos muy tristes por él. Es una lesión corta, pero de un jugador que viene de estar mucho tiempo parado y frena su incorporación y su proceso de adaptación a la competición". El Celta Fortuna está teniendo mala suerte en su temporada histórica de debut en Segunda división, con tres jugadores lesionados de larga duración y algún percance físico menor que ya han sufrido en el primer tercio de la competición.

articles.title: Crystal Palace Women deducted three points in WSL for making substitutions at four windows in Everton win
articles.summary: Crystal Palace Women are being punished for making substitutions at four separate windows in a win over Everton in September - the last of which came in the 97th minute - which is in breach of IFAB Laws that state clubs have no more than three substitution opportunities in each match
articles.body:
Promoted side Palace, who now drop into the relegation play-off spot, are being punished for making substitutions at four separate windows in a 1-0 win over Everton in September.

This is in breach of IFAB Laws, which state clubs can make five substitutions, but have no more than three opportunities in each match to do so.

Palace made a substitution in a fourth window in the 97th minute of the match. Kirsty Howat, who was brought on for Shannon O'Brien, did not touch the ball before the full-time whistle was blown.

Palace admitted to the breach but felt the sanction sought by the WSL was "excessive", according to the written decisions published with the sanction.

However, the independent tribunal determined that a sporting sanction was necessary to avoid damaging the integrity of the competition.

In response, Palace said in a statement on Tuesday: "Everyone at the club is obviously frustrated that such a minor infraction, given that the player was on the pitch for only 46 seconds while the ball was in play, has led to such a significant penalty - a penalty which we do not agree is reasonable or proportionate.

"We are disappointed for the players and staff who worked so hard to secure a deserved victory on our return to the WSL."

Everton's points total is unaffected by the sanction. They remain 11th in the table on 12 points after 11 matches. Palace, meanwhile, drop to second bottom, falling behind Birmingham on goal difference.

How Everton used xG to argue Palace deserved points deduction

Everton disagreed with the assertion of Palace head coach Jo Potter that the outcome of the match was unaffected by their use of a fourth substitution window.

In a letter to the independent tribunal, Everton set out a four-point argument for how the non-compliant substitution had a direct sporting impact on the match.

Everton accumulated seven shots after the 90ᵗʰ minute compared to ten shots prior to the 90ᵗʰ minute; the seven shots were worth 0.49 xG, which is over half the amount Everton had created in the first 90 minutes

Everton had 72 per cent possession after the 90ᵗʰ minute (43 passes vs 17 passes)

Everton had 20 final third passes after the 90ᵗʰ minute, which indicates that Everton were dominant and on top, chasing an equaliser

The fourth substitution came during a period where Everton were clearly on top, breaking up the flow of the match.

Analysis: A 'devastating' punishment for promoted Palace

"Palace did not make an extra substitution but used an extra substitution window, making changes in the 63rd, 83rd, 90th and, crucially, the 97th minute.

"This is devastating for Palace because Kirsty Howat, who came on for Shannon O'Brien, was only on the pitch for a matter of seconds and she didn't touch the ball.

"It is recognised [by the independent tribunal] that this hasn't created any advantage for Palace when it comes to the result, they have to deter other teams from choosing not to adhere to this rule.

"This will be upsetting for Palace, who have dropped down to second bottom in the table. The team in 14th at bottom of the table, currently Charlton, will be immediately relegated.

"Whoever is 13th goes into a play-off against the winner of a match between the second and third team in WSL 2.

"This is gutting for Palace, who were above Birmingham before this deduction. Now they've dropped down and they're in danger. And, mentally, we know how hard it is for promoted teams to stay in the WSL."

articles.title: Duncan Ferguson: Glentoran manager apologises to match officials after being hit with seven-game ban for Cliftonville red
articles.summary: Glentoran manager Duncan Ferguson will be suspended for seven games following his red card in the side's 3-2 defeat by Cliftonville last week.
articles.body:
Glentoran manager Duncan Ferguson has been suspended for seven games following his red card in the side's 3-2 defeat by Cliftonville last week.

The former Everton striker was dismissed for how he addressed match officials after believing the Reds' opener at Solitude should have been ruled out for a foul in the build-up.

The 1995 FA Cup winner arrived at the Oval in October and has so far won one, drawn two and lost one of his four games in charge.

"I want to apologise to the match officials for my behaviour on Friday night," said the former Forest Green Rovers and Inverness Caledonian Thistle boss.

"I was frustrated by what happened on the pitch and let my emotions get the better of me. I went too far in the way I expressed that frustration towards the officials, and I should have handled the situation better."

"I accept the suspension and I'll learn from what happened. My focus now is on the players, the staff and the work we've got to do together, both on and off the pitch."

The sanction will start with Tuesday night's hosting of Larne in the Bet McLean Cup, a competition in which the east Belfast outfit have been beaten finalists the past two seasons.

Even should the Glens progress to the quarter-finals of the competition expected to take place next month, Ferguson's ban would still include the eagerly anticipated Boxing Day visit from fierce rivals Linfield.

articles.title: El Zaragoza supera los triunfos de todo el curso pasado...¡en noviembre!
articles.standfirst: Los maños llevan ya nueve victorias, una más que en toda la 25-26
articles.summary: Los maños llevan ya nueve victorias, una más que en toda la 25-26
articles.body: La victoria del Real Zaragoza frente al Rayo Majadahonda no solo consolidó su liderato, aumentando la renta con el segundo en seis puntos, sino que dejó un dato tremendo. Los maños han alcanzado ya los nueve triunfos en 13 jornadas y han superado las ocho victorias que logró en todo el curso pasado. ¡Y solo estamos en noviembre! La estadística habla maravillas del equipo de Ibai Gómez, que suma 12 encuentros ligueros sin conocer la derrota, y al mismo tiempo deja más en evidencia a la catastrófica campaña pasada que culminó con el descenso tras acabar como colista de Segunda división. Están siendo dos temporadas totalmente opuestas. Desde el inicio las sensaciones fueron horribles hace un año y ahora ocurre todo lo contrario. El Real Zaragoza sabe a lo que juega y ya gana hasta por inercia. Sin brillar, como los grandes, sabe sacar adelante los partidos. Parece que baja del autobús ganando ya 1-0, al revés del curso pasado donde salía derrotado. Ibai y los jugadores han sacado al club y a su afición de la depresión en apenas tres meses de competición. Todavía queda mucho pero la ilusión se ha disparado. El sábado, eso sí, volverán a tener un encuentro muy complicado frente a un Alcorcón en alza que podria ponerse a tres puntos. Pero si los blanquillos cantan la décima darán un nuevo golpe en la mesa.

articles.title: Report Card Grades for Top 20 College Football QBs after Week 12
articles.summary: Every Tuesday morning throughout the 2026 college football season, we will be grading the performance of the top 20 quarterbacks in the nation, then re-ranking a new top 20 for next week's report card assignment.
articles.body:
Every Tuesday morning throughout the 2026 college football season, we will be grading the performance of the top 20 quarterbacks in the nation, then re-ranking a new top 20 for next week's report card assignment.

Included are each player's numbers through the air and on the ground, their game's outcome, and the quality of their opponent. A 1-5 star system was used to highlight the quality of the opponent, using the most recent version of The Athletic's ranking of all 138 FBS teams, with stars awarded as follows:

5 stars: No. 1-10 in the rankings 4 stars: No. 11-40 in the rankings 3 stars: No. 41-70 in the rankings 2 stars: No. 71-100 in the rankings 1 star: No. 101-138 in the rankings or an FCS opponent

Each quarterback's performance was given a grade of A, B, C, D or F. Those grades were factored into the reordering of the rankings for the following week.

After a 2-4 start to the season, Delaware has won four of its last five games, with Minicucci completing 75.5 percent of his passes for 1,675 yards, 18 touchdowns and one interception during that stretch.
