Maddux Madsen threw for 371 yards and four touchdowns in his return from injury against Oregon State in Week 11, but he stumbled on Saturday night with two interceptions and a lost fumble.

Those turnovers played a role in the Broncos suffering their second loss of the season, likely dropping them below Liberty for the top spot among Group of Six teams. Madsen now has a 20-to-3 touchdown-to-interception ratio for the season.

In four games since replacing Will Hammond as Texas Tech's starting quarterback, Thomas Castellanos has thrown for 940 passing yards, rushed for 349 yards and thrown 13 total touchdowns.

A 2,000-yard passer and 1,000-yard rusher at Boston College back in 2023, Castellanos joined Texas Tech in August after spending the summer in mini-camp with the Miami Dolphins. He started at Florida State in 2025.

After a rocky 1-2 start replacing the injured Dante Moore at quarterback, Dylan Raiola has led the Ducks to four straight wins and back to the fringe of the College Football Playoff picture at No. 13 in last week's rankings.

articles.title: B/R's 2026 Heisman Trophy Odds and Rankings after Week 12
articles.summary: The year of the outlier is fast approaching.
articles.body:
The year of the outlier is fast approaching.

When you look through the history of the Heisman Trophy, team success has played a noticeable part in determining the recipient. If a program drops four games, rarely does its star become the award winner.

During the 2026 season, Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith has both individually excelled and benefited from a chaos-filled campaign around him.

But if someone is going to track down Smith at the buzzer—at this point, basically only Darian Mensah or Devon Dampier—team success will play a role.

While the latest FanDuel odds are listed, the rankings are more subjective as a snapshot of this moment in the season.

Bear Bachmeier, QB, BYU : Thanks to losses from UCLA and Indiana, BYU—ranked 10th in last week's CFP Top 25—is flirting with a trip to the College Football Playoff. Especially if that happens, Bachmeier may receive some non-winning votes. He's totaled 2,807 yards and accounted for 27 touchdowns this season.

Charlie Becker, WR, Indiana : Despite the Hoosiers' setback at Washington, Becker continued to build his award profile with six catches for 167 yards and a touchdown. Still holding top-10 potential, Becker has posted 59 receptions for 1,117 yards and 11 scores.

Malachi Toney, WR, Miami : Hurricanes coach Mario Cristobal recently said Toney is "really close" to returning from an ankle injury. Even though the Heisman ship has sailed, Toney may attract a few last-second votes if he's a difference-maker in the ACC Championship Game against Wake Forest.

Jesse Legree, WR, Oregon State : It's reasonable to suggest Legree may find his way onto the back end of some ballots. As a true freshman, he's racked up 78 catches for 1,418 yards and 15 touchdowns.

Keelon Russell, QB, Alabama : Russell won't win the Heisman. He won't be a finalist. But if Week 13 results send Alabama to the SEC Championship Game and the Crimson Tide upset Georgia, he holds top-10 upside. Russell is the most likely of this group to dip below the mark, though.

Nate Sheppard, RB, Duke : Sheppard, meanwhile, is a lock for a share of national recognition. The sophomore has scampered for 1,436 yards and 20 trips to the end zone, adding 46 catches for 402 yards and four more touchdowns— plus a passing score. Duke closes the regular season at Wake Forest, so Sheppard hasn't necessarily reached his ceiling if the Dukies spring an upset.

Gunner Stockton, QB, Georgia : Team success offers a boost for Stockton, who's overseeing the No. 1-ranked Dawgs. However, that should not overshadow a hot finish from the veteran QB. Stockton has climbed to 2,630 offensive yards and 25 total touchdowns. He remains a possible finalist thanks to UGA's extra data point in the SEC Championship Game.

CJ Carr, QB, Notre Dame : Great player. Like, a championship-level QB. Notre Dame is a key contender for the national title. Carr's consistency is a big part of that. Still, his 2,784 yards and 27 total scores trail top candidates like Wake Forest's Gio Lopez—and Lopez will play a 13th contest in the ACC title game.

DeSean Bishop, RB, Tennessee : LSU held Bishop to 65 yards without a score on 20 touches. Nevertheless, the Vols won another game, improved to 9-2 and should make the CFP with a win at Vanderbilt this weekend. Their team's success may vault Bishop into consideration for a string of third-place votes.

Arch Manning, QB, Texas : On paper, the Longhorns have the most favorable paths to the SEC Championship Game compared to Bama and Tennessee. It's a double-edged sword for Manning, who's weathered a midseason storm to put 2,655 yards and 25 touchdowns on his résumé. Knock off Texas A&M and UGA, and Manning will likely command a smattering of votes. He could slip outside the top 10 with a disappointing performance in either matchup.

After cracking the unofficial CFP field in last week's Top 25 at No. 11, Wake Forest is poised to rise again.

Not only did UCLA and Indiana lose in Week 12, BYU needed to survive a triple-overtime game at Kansas. It's entirely plausible the Gio Lopez-led Demon Deacons rise to eighth in Tuesday's update.

The point is simple: Lopez continues to garner more attention.

Given that he's thrown for 2,701 yards with 21 touchdowns and one interception, the increased notice is fully deserved. He's also scampered for 369 yards and 10 scores, propelling Wake to a 10-1 record.

At this point, Lopez is unlikely to win the Heisman. But if the Deacs—who've clinched a rematch with Miami in the ACC Championship Game—topple Duke this weekend, he undoubtedly has finalist upside.

Even if Utah loses to West Virginia, the Utes should be headed to the College Football Playoff. Similarly, Devon Dampier is expected to land as a Heisman Trophy finalist regardless of the WVU result.

Dampier has been a model of consistency, totaling 250-plus yards in nine of Utah's 11 wins and accounting for at least two touchdowns in every game.

Overall, he's passed for 2,535 yards and 24 scores while rushing for 644 yards and 11 scores. Throw in an acrobatic 29-yard reception in the victory over BYU, and Dampier has been a well-rounded weapon for the nation's last unbeaten team.

Dampier is certain to receive a healthy share of votes. He's still a threat to win if the Utes finish 13-0 and win the Big 12 title.

Looking solely at the box score, it may seem that Darian Mensah struggled against Virginia Tech. He wasn't amazing, but he still carried the Hurricanes.

Mensah threw an interception on Miami's opening drive when an accurate throw bounced off a wide-open target's hands. His second interception happened after everyone on the field—including the defender who picked off the pass—thought Virginia Tech had jumped offsides.

Beyond that, he evaded pressure all night behind a struggling UM offensive line. Mensah's ability to extend plays allowed the 'Canes to avoid an upset.

Toney's absence has affected Mensah's numbers, not his impact.

As long as Miami defeats Boston College this weekend, Mensah could sway voters at the last second against Wake Forest in the ACC Championship Game. If Toney is back, that possibility only rises.

Let's be very clear: Jeremiah Smith's existing reputation is a huge factor.

Entering the 2026 campaign, he was already a well-regarded Heisman Trophy contender. Smith was my own prediction back in June, reaffirmed in the preseason . I am absolutely not alone in that, either.

Smith has nearly identical stats to Oregon State's Jesse Legree, but he's a breakout player on an OSU team that isn't in the Top 25. Legree isn't a threat to win.

However, because Smith has matched—even exceeded—expectations for a prominent team, he remains a Heisman contender despite Ohio State's 7-4 record. Not since Oklahoma's Steve Owens in 1969 has a player on a four-loss team hoisted the trophy, yet Smith is a sturdy favorite with two weeks remaining.

Smith, who leads the FBS in receptions, yards and touchdowns with an 86/1,482/17 line, is close to becoming an incredible outlier.

articles.standfirst: Han participado de forma directa en 8 de los últimos 12 goles del equipo
articles.summary: Han participado de forma directa en 8 de los últimos 12 goles del equipo
articles.body: Pacheta ha ido construyendo desde pretemporada un equipo aplicado y solidario, en el que la fuerza del grupo es el principal motor. Pero, más allá de ese rendimiento coral, hay individualidades que sobresalen para impulsar al Granada a un nuevo nivel: piezas clave como Pascual y Alemañ están brillando en este momento dulce de los andaluces. Aunque en Sabadell se truncó la racha de victorias, el Granada acumula una semana más sin perder y ya se ha instalado en la zona de playoffs, gracias, en gran medida, al acierto del atacante almeriense y el centrocampista ilicitano, una dupla que está siendo el motor de los nazaríes en este tramo de la temporada. En estos últimos siete encuentros, Pascual y Alemañ han participado de forma directa, marcando o asistiendo, en 8 de los 12 tantos de los granadinos, lo que supone una implicación vital en el 66% de esas dianas. En la Nova Creu alta, la conexión entre el atacante y el centrocampista volvió a ser fructífera para los rojiblancos. Pascual tiró de calidad para acunar un balón llovido, superar a su par y entregarle el gol en bandeja a su compañero, que llegó desde segunda línea demostrando esa facilidad goleadora que atesora a pesar de ser centrocampistas. Semanas atrás, los papeles se intercambiaron y fue Alemañ el que asistió a Pascual, sellando la victoria ante el Cádiz. Los dos futbolistas han sabido digerir momentos de menos protagonismo en el arranque de la competición para esperar su momento y recuperar la mejor versión en un pasaje decisivo para los rojiblancos.

articles.title: Quadri renueva con el Sabadell hasta 2029
articles.standfirst: El equipo arlequinado se asegura la continuidad de uno de sus jugadores más cotizados
articles.summary: El equipo arlequinado se asegura la continuidad de uno de sus jugadores más cotizados
articles.body: El Sabadell ha alegrado un frío martes de noviembre a su afición con una noticia excelente: Quadri Liameed, uno de los jugadores más cotizados del equipo de Ferran Costa, ha renovado su contrato por dos temporadas más, hasta el año 2029. El mediocentro nigeriano acababa contrato en junio, por lo que era libre de firmar con cualquier equipo a partir del 1 de enero, pero las dos partes han querido seguir unidas. El club de la Nova Creu Alta ha anunciado la renovación con un mensaje inequívoco: La historia continúa. La historia arlequinada de Quadri comenzó hace apenas un año y medio, cuando recaló en la ciudad procedente del Lleida. Antes había jugado en el equipo juvenil del Villarreal. "En poco más de una temporada se ha ganado el corazón de todos los arlequinados con su fútbol, su carácter y su compromiso con el club. Con esta renovación, el club se asegura la continuidad de un futbolista en pleno crecimiento y de un referente para la afición", reivindica el comunicado del club. Quadri, de 24 años, ha jugado 56 encuentros con el Sabadell y la temporada pasada fue el MVP de los playoffs de ascenso. Esta temporada sigue siendo clave e imprescindible, un fijo. Fue titular en las primeras 13 jornadas, pero se ha perdido los dos últimos duelos por el duro golpe en la cabeza que recibió en el encuentro del 31 de octubre con el Albacete. Corpas golpeó su cabeza con mucha fuerza en un intento de remate y el jugador de Lagos cayó desplomado sobre el campo, inconsciente. Se vivieron escenas de gran preocupación y tuvo que ser evacuado del terreno de juego en ambulancia y trasladado de urgencia a un hospital. Reapareció en la jornada siguiente, contra la Real Sociedad B, pero tuvo que ser sustituido a los 12 minutos porque se mareó. Se ha perdido los partidos con el Eldense y el Granada y podría regresar a la convocatoria para el partido de este viernes en Leganés.

articles.body: Con los tres goles al Oviedo, el Córdoba disfrutó durante unas horas de ser el equipo más goleador de LaLiga Hypermotion. 28 goles en 15 encuentros, una media de 1,87 sencillamente tremenda para el rol del cuadro califal en la categoría, ahora mismo en la zona media de la tabla. Pero esos datos, acercándose a la media de dos tantos por partido, no sólo destacan a nivel español. Si se miran las segundas categorías de las cinco grandes Ligas de Europa (Inglaterra, Italia, España, Alemania y Francia), Almería y Córdoba brillan con luz propia. El conjunto rojiblanco comparte el quinto puesto con Hertha Berlín y el Wolfsburgo de la Bundesliga 2. Mientras, el conjunto de Iván Ania es el octavo de esas Ligas, empatado con Wolverhampton, Birmingham y Cardiff, todos de la Championship. Aun así, hay que matizar que en esa lista, que encabezan en el guarismo total precisamente otros cuatro conjuntos de la segunda categoría inglesa, caso de West Ham (38), Norwich (34), Middlesbrough (32) y Southampton (31), es más realista si se acude a la media, ya que no todas las competiciones disputaron el mismo número de jornadas. Ahí, los datos de los dos conjuntos andaluces bajan algo, pero también rozan el Top 10 entre estas Segundas que, en realidad, podrían estar por delante por potencial de otras Primeras en países europeos en un segundo escalón. El promedio del Almería es, con 1,93, el 11º de estas competiciones de referencia, mientras el Córdoba le sigue con el 12º puesto con el citado 1,87, justo delante del Castellón (1,86). articles.title: World Cup and Clarkson partnership drove profit surge, says Marston's
articles.summary: The company says an "excellent World Cup" helped drive strong trading as annual profits rose by 18%.
articles.body:
Pub company Marston's has said an "excellent World Cup" helped drive stronger trading as annual profits rose by nearly a fifth, despite reporting a dip in sales .

The Wolverhampton-based firm, which operates more than 1,300 pubs across the UK, reported underlying pre-tax profits of £85.4m for the year to 26 September, up 18.4% from a year earlier.

The company said trading was improved by new-look pubs, strong trade during this summer's football World Cup, and a partnership with Jeremy Clarkson's Hawkstone drinks brand.

"For the third year running, profit is significantly up, cash flow is strong and margins have improved," said chief executive Justin Platt.

The pub chain also said bookings for Christmas events were 9% ahead of the same point last year.

Marston's has invested heavily in refurbishing pubs into new formats, including its sports-focused "Grandstand" venues.

It plans at least 100 more conversions in the new financial year, in a bid to accelerate sales growth further.

One of the busiest locals during the World Cup was The New Spires in Coventry, which reopened in March following a £400,000 makeover.

The World Cup had been "very full on," said pub partner Pip Sullivan, explaining that on one match night alone they took more than £25,000 over the bar.

Marston's said it had selected the venue for investment because of its involvement with local sports teams, community groups, and charities.

"We've got two football teams, four darts teams and a dominoes team," explained Sullivan, all of which had also helped bolster sales.

But she recognised not all businesses were thriving.

"It's been a difficult year for a lot of pubs and we have empathised as they've lost a lot of trade," she said.

But investment by the company had brought the pub "back to life", she continued.

"We've managed to keep as much custom as we possibly can and seen new custom."

Marston's also pointed to events and promotions, including darts champion Luke Humphries' darts nights and the partnership with Clarkson.

"Guest satisfaction levels have improved again, thanks to the amazing work of our pub teams, whose passion and commitment keep our pubs at the heart of every local community they serve," added Platt.

"Our new pub formats are performing especially well and are now a proven growth engine for the business, giving us real confidence to accelerate our investment plans in 2027."

articles.summary: El lateral del PSG evita pronunciarse sobre el proceso judicial por una presunta violación y asegura que su única prioridad es el fútbol y el duelo de Champions frente al Roma
articles.body: El jugador hispano-marroquí del París Saint-Germain Achraf Hakimi declinó este martes valorar el juicio que enfrentará en 2027 como presunto autor de una violación en 2023 y aseguró que ahora está "concentrado en el fútbol", comenzando por el partido de mañana de Liga de Campeones ante el AS Roma. "Estoy concentrado en el fútbol, que es lo más importante para mí. Eso no me impide hacer mi juego. Ya veremos en el futuro; estoy centrado en el partido de mañana y en mi oficio, que es el fútbol", declaró Hakimi, en la conferencia de prensa previa al choque en París ante el Roma italiano. El pasado septiembre, la Justicia francesa confirmó que el internacional marroquí, de 28 años, será juzgado, en una fecha de 2027 aún por detallar, por el cargo de violación. El jugador fue acusado de violación en febrero de 2023 por una joven que acudió a su domicilio en la localidad de Boulogne-Billancourt, a las afueras de París, tras más de un mes de intercambios de mensajes a través de las redes sociales. Según su denuncia, el futbolista la besó en los labios pese a su rechazo, le levantó la ropa y le besó los senos e incluso le introdujo los dedos en la vagina, a pesar de su resistencia. La chica, entonces de 24 años, señaló que consiguió deshacerse de su agresor de una patada y envió un mensaje a una amiga, que acudió a buscarla. Hakimi ha negado desde el principio cualquier acto de penetración, admitiendo únicamente abrazos mutuos e intercambios de besos consentidos. Para apuntalar su relato, la defensa presentó el testimonio de su amigo Kylian Mbappé -hoy en el Real Madrid en la época de los hechos denunciados en el PSG-, con quien el marroquí había hablado la noche de los hechos y que fue interrogado por los investigadores el 14 de abril de 2023

articles.title: Juanfran Funes seguirá... de momento
articles.standfirst: El técnico dependerá de la elección del nuevo entrenador
articles.summary: El técnico dependerá de la elección del nuevo entrenador
articles.body: La salida de Loren Juarros del Málaga CF será oficial esta misma semana. La gran incógnita ahora está en el banquillo y tiene un nombre propio: Juanfran Funes. El todavía director deportivo conoce la decisión del club desde el pasado lunes, cuando se produjo una reunión entre todas las partes. Una vez aclarado su futuro, Kike Pérez y José María Muñoz pusieron rumbo a Madrid para asistir a la gala del CTA. La etapa de Loren en Martiricos está sentenciada, pero todavía queda por definir qué sucederá con el entrenador. La intención del Málaga, como ya adelantó Radio MARCA Málaga, es que el nuevo director deportivo tenga la última palabra sobre la continuidad del preparador de Loja. En el club todavía confían en Funes y consideran que una serie de incorporaciones puede cambiar el rumbo del equipo. Sin embargo, también asumen que el próximo responsable de la parcela deportiva pueda querer configurar su propio proyecto, algo que podría incluir un cambio en el banquillo. En estos momentos, Mikel Martija es el principal favorito para asumir la dirección deportiva blanquiazul. Su perfil, con una trayectoria similar a la de Juarros en el trabajo con la cantera, y su profundo conocimiento del mercado de Segunda División y Primera RFEF juegan a su favor. Esas características le sitúan por delante del resto de aspirantes, aunque Nico Rodríguez también cuenta con muchos apoyos. Su buena relación con Kike Pérez es uno de los factores que le mantienen en la carrera. Mientras tanto, el vestuario ha mantenido públicamente una postura de respaldo tanto a Loren Juarros como a Juanfran Funes. No han trascendido discrepancias ni reproches, aunque puertas adentro sí existe preocupación por el estado anímico de una plantilla muy castigada por la situación deportiva. El nuevo director deportivo tendrá sobre la mesa la decisión más importante de las próximas semanas: apostar por la continuidad de Funes o iniciar una nueva etapa también en el banquillo.

articles.title: Scottish FA lead tributes as former president George Peat dies aged 86
articles.summary: Former Scottish FA president George Peat dies at the age of 86.
articles.body:
Former Scottish FA president George Peat has died at the age of 86.

The former Airdrieonians and Stenhousemuir director spent four years in the role, taking over from John McBeth in 2007.

He oversaw the appointments of Scotland managers George Burley and Craig Levein and commissioned former first minister Henry McLeish to conduct a review of Scottish football.

Peat was also at the helm when Scottish referees opted to take strike action in November 2010.

"George loved his football and was renowned as a forthright personality and formidable negotiator but behind that imposing exterior lay a sharp wit and a glint in his eye," said current SFA president Mike Mulraney.

"He cared deeply about the national game and his beloved Airdrieonians.

"George was also passionate about the modernisation of the association and commissioned the McLeish Review of Scottish football as one of his first acts as president.

"He was a regular visitor to Hampden, even as his health deteriorated, and will be sadly missed by his friends and former colleagues at the Scottish FA and across the game."

articles.title: ¡Insólito! el Crystal Palace femenino pierde tres puntos por un error... en los cambios
articles.standfirst: El conjunto londinense incumplió la normativa al utilizar una cuarta ventana de sustituciones ante el Everton y pierde los puntos logrados en aquella victoria
articles.summary: El conjunto londinense incumplió la normativa al utilizar una cuarta ventana de sustituciones ante el Everton y pierde los puntos logrados en aquella victoria
articles.body: El Crystal Palace Women ha recibido uno de los castigos más llamativos de la temporada en la Women's Super League (WSL). El conjunto londinense ha sido sancionado con una deducción de tres puntos después de incumplir la normativa de sustituciones durante su victoria por 1-0 frente al Everton en septiembre. El motivo de la sanción no fue una alineación indebida ni un problema administrativo, sino un error en la gestión de los cambios. El equipo dirigido por Jo Potter realizó sustituciones en cuatro ventanas distintas a lo largo del encuentro, cuando el reglamento únicamente permite tres oportunidades de cambios durante el partido, sin contar el descanso. La infracción se produjo en el tiempo añadido, cuando Kirsty Howat sustituyó a Shannon O'Brien en el minuto 97. La futbolista apenas permaneció unos segundos sobre el terreno de juego y ni siquiera llegó a tocar el balón antes del pitido final. Tras investigar lo sucedido, un tribunal independiente concluyó que el error fue involuntario y que el Crystal Palace Women no trató de obtener una ventaja deportiva. Sin embargo, también consideró que mantener el resultado sin castigo dañaría la credibilidad de la competición, por lo que optó por retirar los tres puntos logrados en aquel encuentro. El Everton, por su parte, no recibirá esos puntos y el duelo no será repetido. La resolución supone un duro golpe para el recién ascendido conjunto inglés. La deducción le hace caer hasta la zona de peligro de la clasificación y complica notablemente su lucha por la permanencia. El club mostró su malestar tras conocerse la decisión y calificó el castigo de desproporcionado, insistiendo en que la jugadora implicada solo estuvo sobre el césped durante 46 segundos y sin participar en ninguna acción del juego. Aun así, la sanción es firme y no admite recurso. El panel señaló que la infracción fue involuntaria, no tenía la intención de obtener una ventaja injusta y fue aprobada por los oficiales del partido ese mismo día. Obviamente, en el club todos estamos frustrados de que una infracción tan leve, teniendo en cuenta que el jugador estuvo en el terreno de juego solo 46 segundos mientras el balón estaba en juego, haya dado lugar a una sanción tan importante, una sanción que no consideramos razonable ni proporcionada. Sentimos mucha pena por las jugadoras y el cuerpo técnico que trabajaron tan duro para conseguir una merecida victoria en nuestro regreso a la WSL.

articles.title: Uganda esconde un 'mini Kanté' de 15 años que deslumbra en el Mundial
articles.standfirst: Henry Muhoozi, elegido mejor jugador ante Ecuador, pasó de ser descubierto por un ojeador en su colegio a convertirse en una de las grandes promesas ugandesas. Su fútbol ya despierta interés entre los observadores presentes en Catar
articles.summary: Henry Muhoozi, elegido mejor jugador ante Ecuador, pasó de ser descubierto por un ojeador en su colegio a convertirse en una de las grandes promesas ugandesas. Su fútbol ya despierta interés entre los observadores presentes en Catar
articles.body: Una visita inesperada a un colegio del sur de Uganda cambió la vida de Henry Muhoozi. Mark Namanya, un captador de talentos que recorría las escuelas en busca de jóvenes futbolistas para una academia de Mbarara, encontró en el Wagwa Memorial Primary School a un niño que ni siquiera había pensado demasiado en dedicarse al fútbol. Vio en él algo especial. Le ofreció marcharse para continuar su formación y, con el consentimiento de su madre, el pequeño hizo las maletas. Aquel viaje desde Lukaya, su localidad natal, terminó llevándolo hasta un Mundial. Hoy, con 15 años, es uno de los nombres que despiertan interés entre los scouts que recorren los campos del Aspire Zone de Doha. Y en Uganda ya tienen un apodo para él: el 'mini Kanté'. La comparación con el francés nació durante una concentración de las categorías inferiores ugandesas en Dire Dawa, Etiopía. Allí empezaron a llamarlo 'Ng'oro Kanté', por su serenidad, su inteligencia táctica y esa particular facilidad para aparecer donde va a caer el balón. Muhoozi mide 1,70 metros, pero compensa su falta de envergadura con una lectura del juego poco habitual a su edad. Anticipa las líneas de pase, recupera balones y se mueve con agilidad en espacios reducidos. Su bajo centro de gravedad le permite girarse bajo presión y superar rivales mediante la conducción. No es únicamente un futbolista dedicado a destruir el juego contrario. También tiene criterio para organizar el propio, aunque todavía necesita ganar fortaleza en los duelos y mejorar su desplazamiento en largo. Lo curioso es que Muhoozi no siempre fue mediocentro. Cuando Laryea Kingston comenzó a trabajar con él, ocupaba posiciones más ofensivas. Fue el seleccionador quien decidió retrasarlo hasta la base del centro del campo, convencido de que allí podría aprovechar mejor sus cualidades. "Necesitaba a alguien que supiera cuidar el balón en espacios reducidos y hacer que sucedieran cosas. De los 66 futbolistas que evalué, ninguno podía desempeñar mejor ese papel", explicó el técnico. Una apuesta que inicialmente despertó dudas, pero que terminó convirtiéndolo en el cerebro de Uganda. "Mi número seis tiene que ser excelente con el balón. Él encaja en esa descripción. Es inteligente, cuida la pelota y tiene un gran futuro", añadió Kingston. Detrás de ese futbolista hay una historia familiar. Henry es el segundo de seis hermanos y creció en Lukaya, en la región de Masaka. Su madre, Faridah Nakanwagi, fue determinante para que pudiera abandonar su entorno y trasladarse a Mbarara, donde ingresó en la Alfa Soccer Academy. Después llegaron otros centros educativos, los torneos escolares y nuevas oportunidades para progresar. "Les debo muchísimo. Siempre me han apoyado. Todavía no he llegado a ser lo que quiero, porque me queda un largo camino, pero sé que trabajaré duro para conseguirlo", reconoció Muhoozi en una entrevista publicada por la Federación Ugandesa de Fútbol. En ese camino también aparece Musa Ssuna, su primo materno. Los dos coincidieron en el Amus College School, compartieron formación y llegaron a competir por el mismo puesto en el centro del campo. Una rivalidad familiar a la que la propia federación ugandesa dedicó un reportaje. Ssuna, más expresivo y comunicativo; Muhoozi, de carácter reservado. Dos personalidades diferentes que terminaron encontrándose también en las categorías inferiores de su país. Ahora comparten una experiencia que pocos jóvenes de su entorno pueden contar: disputar un Mundial con Uganda. Su progresión comenzó a recibir reconocimientos antes de aterrizar en Catar. Muhoozi fue elegido mejor jugador del Campeonato CECAFA Sub-17 de 2026, conquistado por Uganda, y se consolidó como una de las piezas fundamentales de su generación. El Mundial le ha permitido dar el siguiente paso. Después de caer ante Corea del Sur en el estreno, Uganda consiguió un empate sin goles frente a Ecuador en un encuentro que tuvo al centrocampista como protagonista. En el minuto 55 ejecutó una falta directa que terminó estrellándose contra el larguero. Le faltaron unos centímetros para marcar, pero no para llevarse el reconocimiento al mejor jugador del partido. Un premio que confirmó las buenas sensaciones que está dejando ante los observadores desplazados al torneo. "Conseguir este reconocimiento significa mucho para mí. En un torneo de este nivel hay muchos buenos futbolistas, así que recibir este premio me da mucha motivación", explicó Muhoozi después de enfrentarse a Ecuador. No quiso, sin embargo, detenerse demasiado en el reconocimiento individual. "No queremos quedarnos en la fase de grupos, queremos llegar lejos. Para conseguirlo tenemos que seguir trabajando muy duro", añadió. También agradeció el apoyo de los aficionados ugandeses que han acompañado al equipo en Doha, incluso después de la derrota inicial. "Perdimos el primer partido y, aun así, han vuelto para animarnos. Eso demuestra que quieren mucho a esta selección y se lo agradecemos enormemente". Muhoozi admira a Kevin De Bruyne y al internacional ugandés Allan Okello. Sueña con jugar algún día en una gran liga europea, aunque todavía le queda un largo recorrido por delante. En la lista oficial de FIFA figura como jugador del Arsenal College FC, después de haberse formado en el fútbol escolar de su país. Su progresión dependerá ahora de cómo responda al salto físico y competitivo que exige la élite. De momento, ha conseguido algo que parecía lejano cuando aquel captador entró en su colegio de Lukaya. Entonces necesitó que un ojeador fuera a buscarlo. Ahora son los ojeadores quienes se acercan para verlo jugar.

articles.title: Millwall forced to partially close the Den after commission proves FA charges of discriminatory chanting
articles.summary: Millwall have been punished for discriminatory chanting relating to disability and sexual orientation by fans in a game against Charlton in January; a two-game partial stadium closure (one game of which is suspended) is first of its kind at this level; Millwall also fined £70,000
articles.body:
The unprecedented measure is for Millwall failing to ensure their supporters didn't engage in discriminatory chanting that includes reference to disability and sexual orientation during a home match with Charlton in January.

As well as a two-game partial stadium closure - one game of which is suspended until the end of the 2027/28 season - Millwall have been fined £70,000 plus hearing costs, warned about their future conduct, and have had their FA Action Plan extended until the end of next season.

Blocks 19, 20, 47 and 48 of the Dockers Stand will be closed when Millwall host Sheffield United on December 8 - a total of 1,274 seats.

In their written conclusions, the commission found "the club's degree of culpability in relation to the incidents was significant".

In response, speaking exclusively to Sky Sports , Millwall managing director Mark Fairbrother said: "As a club, we didn't do enough and on behalf of the club I apologise to everyone who has been affected by that chanting because it shouldn't happen."

Millwall pleaded guilty to the charges but Fairbrother said Millwall were "disappointed" with the outcome.

He also pointed to new processes the club have since put in place to try to avoid a recurrence - but called on other football clubs, the FA, and organisations such as Kick It Out to come together to find preventative solutions.

"We challenge everything we do and look at if there are ways that we can improve? It's highlighted where we need to be better," he said. "We had already put mitigations in place and need to continue to do so.

"But this is one football club. These instances are happening across football. This is a challenge for the sport in general.

"We see it this [past] week with the charges to Chelsea and also the FA for the England fans in Spain . So, we can put measures in place but we're one club. We can't solve all of society's issues.

"We need to work with all key football stakeholders to look at how can we all do this better? What does good look like? What does best practice look like? And making sure that we embrace that. But everyone else has a collective responsibility as well."

Fairbrother says "the stick approach" used against clubs whose supporters are found guilty of discriminatory chanting just "punishes the fans who actually are just here to enjoy themselves". Instead, he asks "what can we do in terms of the carrot approach to educate people to eradicate this?"

He also noted that supporters identified in the discriminatory chanting against Charlton were all under 18 years old.

"That shows a lack of understanding of the implication of these words," he said. "These words obviously hurt and they have a significant impact on those groups that it affects. But there's that lack of understanding of the issue and the impact."

Asked if he would be interested in working more with groups such as Kick It Out to address this aspect, Fairbrother said: "I'd embrace it. From a personal perspective, I think that would be really good and I implore them to please come work with us, come and look at what we do, challenge what we do.

"If you don't think something we're doing is good enough, come and tell us but look at solutions. If we all have a solutions-focused mindset, we can actually start to make real difference."

The regulatory commission also wrote in their conclusions that "the reputation of the club and English football would have been tarnished" by the chanting during a game shown live on Sky Sports . Fairbrother feels that.

"It hurts all of us in the club. But I know it hurts our fans as well because that is not who we are," he said.

Millwall play Charlton again at the Den on December 19 in a Championship fixture. On how the club are working to avoid a repeat of the discriminatory chanting heard in January, Fairbrother said: "We've put in place a number of procedures already.

"We've already had West Ham here earlier in the season, which was probably our highest-risk fixture for a number of years. That went without incident. But we had a different approach to different fan groups in terms of just reminding them of their responsibility.

"But also for us as a club, making sure that we're on the front foot in terms of everything we do. We will have that same approach to Charlton. You can't predict the future, but we have a more robust process in place now."

This latest issue was the first case of discriminatory chanting at the Den since an FA Cup tie with Everton in 2019 - but follows three other cases involving Millwall supporters away from home since April 2023.

Asked whether he is confident of making a difference, Fairbrother said that would require the support of Millwall fans to call out discriminatory language.

"For each of those instances - and all three of them were away games - there were specific small fan groups who obviously engaged with that chanting. This is now the first instance we've had here at the Den," he said.

"So for all fans, we need to check and challenge this. We need to make sure it doesn't build up. Don't engage with this type of chanting.

"It's not fair on [other Millwall supporters]. We need to all do better. As a club, we need to do better and we will do better for them. But also, it's a collective one. If it happens, if people see it, call it out. We all need to be more proactive on this.

"I'm proud to represent Millwall and I think it goes against what this club's really about."

Sky Sports News has contacted the FA and Kick It Out for comment

articles.title: Luis Enrique descarta ir al mercado de invierno
articles.standfirst: A pesar de graves lesiones de Doué y Kvaratshelia
articles.summary: A pesar de graves lesiones de Doué y Kvaratshelia
articles.body: Luis Enrique, entrenador del París Saint-Germain (PSG), descartó acudir al mercado de inverno a pesar de las reciente lesiones de dos de sus puntales ofensivos: Desiré Doué y Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, quienes estarán de baja varios meses por respectivas lesiones de rodilla. "No tenemos la obligación de acudir al mercado, no vamos a fichar a un jugador para seis meses, no es nuestro estilo. Tenemos un equipo", declaró Luis Enrique, en la conferencia de prensa previa al choque en París ante el Roma italiano. "Es verdad que hay que estar más atentos, pero con estos jugadores, este cuerpo técnico y esta afición no tenemos miedo a nada. Confiamos en hacer nuestro trabajo y superar las dificultades", agregó. El PSG, líder de la primera fase de la Champions con cuatro victorias en otros tantos partidos, empatado a puntos con el Real Madrid, se mide a la Roma, que es vigésima en la tabla, cerca de los puestos de eliminación. Luis Enrique elogió a su homólogo de la Roma, el veterano Gian Piero Gasperini (68 años), y a los delanteros del club italiano, entre ellos el neerlandés Donyell Malen, quien acaba de marcar cuatro goles en la serie A ante el Parma (1-5), y ya suma 16 en todas las competiciones en lo que va de temporada. "Conocemos a todos los jugadores de la Roma, sobre todo a los delanteros. Antes Malen jugaba en banda y, cuando pasó al centro, demostró su capacidad para marcar goles. Su cifra de goles es increíble", indicó. Luis Enrique entrenó a la Roma hace 15 años, una breve etapa que le marcó, a pesar de la falta de buenos resultados. "Fue muy especial para mí. Tengo un buen recuerdo de mi año en Roma. Es una sensación muy bonita cada vez que tengo la posibilidad de visitar Roma, es magnífico. Las cosas pueden ir mejor o peor, pero así es la vida. Hay que aceptarlo. Guardo un recuerdo muy positivo", cerró.

articles.title: Senegal crowned AFCON 2025 champions by Court of Arbitration for Sport following appeal
articles.summary: An announcement confirmed CAS determined Senegal to be the winners of the tournament, which concluded in January; Senegal beat Morocco 1-0 in the final, but were stripped of the title in March, which led to their appeal
articles.body:
Senegal beat Morocco 1-0 in the final in January, but were stripped of the title by a Confederation of African Football (CAF) Appeal Board in March for breaking competition rules by walking off the pitch because of a late disallowed goal and a controversial penalty award.

Senegal's protest caused a delay of 15 minutes, and when their players returned to the pitch, Morocco's Brahim Diaz missed the penalty to force the match into extra time.

"The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) has upheld the appeal by the Senegalese Football Federation (FSF) against the Confederation of African Football (CAF) and the the Royal Moroccan Football Federation (FRMF, in French) concerning the final of the Africa Cup of Nations Morocco 2025 (AFCON 2025)," a CAS statement read.

"The decision rendered by the CAF Appeal Board is set aside and the decision by the CAF Disciplinary Board is reinstated. Consequently, the result obtained at the end of the AFCON 2025 final is confirmed (1-0 for Senegal)."

Morocco's appeal was initially rejected but a CAF panel did uphold it and found Senegal's walk-off meant they had forfeited the match, awarding a 3-0 win to Morocco.

Senegal then appealed to CAS, calling the decision "a travesty," and have now been reinstated as champions.

Morocco's initial appeal was rejected but a CAF panel did uphold it and found Senegal's walk-off meant they had forfeited the match, awarding a 3-0 win to Morocco.

CAF said Senegal infringed on article 82 of AFCON's regulations, which states if a team refuses to play or leaves the ground before the end of regulation time without the refereee's authorisation, it will be considered the loser and eliminated from the competition.

Article 84 states any team that violates article 82 will be permanently eliminated and lose the match 3-0.

'Common sense prevails' but is this really over?

Sky Sports News' Chief Correspondent Kaveh Solhekol:

"Common sense has prevailed because the Court of Arbitration for Sport have effectively confirmed that Senegal did win the 2025 AFCON.

"Morocco were very unhappy because they felt that the rules of the tournament had been broken by Senegal when they left the pitch. They felt that at that stage Senegal should have forfeited the game.

"They went to the African Confederation Appeal Board and there was an appeal hearing in March. That appeal decided that yes, Morocco were right and they should be the winners and the result of the game was changed from a 1-0 win to Senegal to a 3-0 win to Morocco.

"Then we had the next chapter in this story because Senegal were also very unhappy with the decision of the appeal board, so they went to CAS in Switzerland. There was a hearing in October and now we have had the decision - a unanimous decision from the three judges.

"I don't want to tempt fate, because let's wait and see what the Moroccan Federation say, but what I would say to you is that they have fought this all the way, they believe that this is an injustice and they are one of the most powerful football associations in Africa.

"They are co-hosts of the next World Cup in 2030 and they have a very close relationships with the leadership at FIFA.

"I'm not suggesting that anything untoward is going on, but they still do have options. For instance, if they feel there has been something wrong in the procedures at the CAS hearing, they could go to the Swiss Federal Tribunal.

"I think the Moroccan Federation, according to what Reuters are reporting this afternoon, are unhappy with the way CAS handled this appeal and they have complained to CAS because they believe that one of the judges actually spoke on the phone to the president of the Senegal Federation on Sunday afternoon, so perhaps that is an avenue that they are going to explore."

'Unanimous decision' - CAS statement in full

The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) has upheld the appeal by the Senegalese Football Federation (FSF) against the Confederation of African Football (CAF) and the the Royal Moroccan Football Federation (FRMF, in French) concerning the final of the Africa Cup of Nations Morocco 2025 (AFCON 2025).

The decision rendered by the CAF Appeal Board is set aside and the decision by the CAF Disciplinary Board is reinstated. Consequently, the result obtained at the end of the AFCON 2025 final is confirmed (1-0 for Senegal).

The FSF appealed to CAS against a decision of the CAF Appeal Board declaring that the Senegal national team forfeited the AFCON 2025 final and recording the Moroccan national team as the winners.

In their appeal, the FSF argued that the decision of the Referee, Mr Jean-Jacques Ngambo Ndala, to resume the match at the 109th minute (90+19) during the AFCON 2025 final and to allow it to be concluded with a sporting result could not be reviewed, pursuant to the 'field of play' doctrine.

The FRMF argued, on the contrary, that the Referee's decision did not fall under the 'field of play' doctrine, as it cannot be applicable to the disciplinary consequences of the Senegalese team's behaviour. The FRMF alleged that, by leaving the pitch temporarily, the Senegalese team breached Articles 82 and 84 of the AFCON Regulations, which should have led the Referee to bring the match to an early conclusion. The FRMF also argued that the Referee erred in law and that his decision was arbitrary.

After having examined the arguments raised by the Parties, the Arbitral Panel considered that the Referee's decision to resume the match or to stop it fell definitively within his sole authority. By blowing his whistle to restart play, the Referee considered that the conditions for resuming the match had been met - both teams were on the pitch again, and both expressed their willingness to resume.

In the Panel's view, there is no doubt that the effects of the Referee's decision were limited to the pitch. As such, the Panel considers that the Referee's decision was covered by the 'field of play' doctrine. Since Articles 82 and 84 of the AFCON Regulations are intended solely to determine the outcome of a match when a team's conduct leads the referee to call off the game permanently, they are therefore not applicable in this case. In conclusion, the Panel considers that in resuming the match, the Referee did not err in law.

The Panel acknowledged that the Referee had to make a decision in an atmosphere of extreme tension. However, these circumstances do not justify describing the decision as "arbitrary". On the contrary, the Referee's judgment did not appear to have been affected by factors external to the game.

Regarding the disciplinary aspects of the case, the Panel noted that the FSF, the FSF coach Mr. Pape Thiaw, and certain players had already been sanctioned by CAF following separate disciplinary proceedings.

Consequently, the appeal by the FSF was upheld. This was a unanimous decision by the CAS Panel.

articles.title: El TAS 'recupera' la Copa África para Senegal... y Marruecos se enciende
articles.standfirst: Confirma la victoria del equipo de Mané en la edición de 2025
articles.summary: Confirma la victoria del equipo de Mané en la edición de 2025
articles.body: El TAS (Tribunal de Arbitraje Deportivo) ha resuelto que 'devuelve' la Copa África 2025 a Senegal, revocando la decisión que en marzo la CAF tomó y ratificando así lo que pasó en el campo: el triunfo senegalés por 0-1. Esta decisión del TAS ha encendido a Marruecos, que ayer, como publicamos en MARCA, esperaba "al 99,9%" un fallo favorable del TAS. No ha sido así finalmente. "El Tribunal de Arbitraje Deportivo (TAS) ha confirmado la apelación presentada por la Federación Senegalesa de Fútbol (FSF) contra la Confederación Africana de Fútbol (CAF) y la Real Federación Marroquí de Fútbol (FRMF, en francés) en relación con la final de la Copa Africana de Naciones Marruecos 2025 (AFCON 2025). La decisión emitida por la Junta de Apelación de la CAF queda anulada y la decisión de la Junta Disciplinaria de la CAF se restablece. En consecuencia, el resultado obtenido al final de la final de la AFCON 2025 se confirma (1-0 a favor de Senegal)", dicta el comunica oficial. Recordemos que a mediado de marzo, la CAF le retiró el título a Senegal, que había ganado la finalísima de enero gracias a un gol de Pape Gueye (0-1) en la prórroga. Luego vinieron las denuncias de la Federación marroquí alegando que los 'Leones de la Teranga', durante la prórroga, habían abandonado el encuentro tras pitar el árbitro un dudoso penalti a favor de Marruecos que Brahim tiró 'a lo Panenka' tras estar el partido parado 15 minutos por el abandono senegalés. BD lo falló y el partido lo ganó Senegal finalmente. "Si, por cualquier motivo, un equipo se niega a jugar o abandona el terreno de juego antes del final reglamentario del partido sin la autorización del árbitro será considerado el perdedor y quedará eliminado de la competición en curso", establecía el Artículo 82 de la CAN. En virtud de ese artículo, la CAF revocó el resultado automáticamente y se le dio como ganado a Marruecos por 0-3 en marzo pasado. Ahora el TAS vuelve a decidir a favor de Senegal. Tras aquel 3-0 en los despachos, Senegal, como no podía ser de otro modo, emitió alegaciones para conservar el título y apeló la decisión impuesta al TAS. "Es injusto, sin precedentes e inaceptable", llegó a pronunciar su Federación, que ahora ve cómo el TAS le da la razón. Durante todos estos meses, el Tribunal Superior de Arbitraje Deportivo ha estudiado el caso, y abandonar el campo no es razón jurídica para darle el título a Marruecos, por lo que Senegal mantiene la corona ganada en el césped. La polémica seguirá con esta Copa 2025.

Brighton and Hove Albion suffered a disappointing 2-0 defeat against Hull City on Sunday, creating a blip in their impressive recent Premier League form.

Despite enjoying several promising spells and creating numerous chances in an attempt to put the game to bed, the Seagulls were unable to find a way past an inspired Konstantinos Tzolakis.

However, Oli McBurnie subsequently struck twice in stoppage time to secure a last minute victory for the Tigers.

Despite this, the scoreline doesn't tell the entire story.

Here are Albion's player ratings from a tough afternoon in Yorkshire.

Replaced during the second half as Hürzeler looked to introduce additional attacking options.

Although the Seagulls lacked the finishing touch, Groß continued to demonstrate why his creativity remains important.

A hardworking display from the Spaniard, who provided energy and defensive cover.

However, his influence faded as the contest progressed, with the visitors struggling to maintain their earlier control during the closing stages.

Although his movement was impressive, he will be disappointed not to have converted at least one of his chances.

His deliveries caused problems for Hull's defence, including an excellent ball that presented Gómez with a clear chance.

One of Brighton's brighter attacking outlets, despite the disappointing result.

He looked determined to make an impact, but Georginio Rutter was unsuccessful in his attempts to break the deadlock.

He forced Tzolakis into several saves and reacted quickly when Ayari's effort struck the crossbar.

However, like several of his teammates, he was unable to produce the decisive finish Albion needed.

He was replaced during the second half as Hürzeler searched for a breakthrough.

Introduced in the second half to provide fresh energy in midfield.

The academy graduate helped maintain possession and offered movement in attacking areas, although he struggled to significantly influence the outcome.

Added pace and directness following his introduction.

The winger looked to stretch Hull's defensive structure, but opportunities became increasingly limited as the match progressed.

A useful attacking option, although he couldn't provide the breakthrough Brighton needed

The young Greek forward brought energy and movement to the attack after replacing Rutter.

He managed to find himself in dangerous positions and went close during a goalmouth scramble.

However, he couldn't turn those opportunities into a goal.

Replaced Gómez with around ten minutes remaining.

He offered fresh legs and attempted to support Brighton's forward efforts, but his introduction came shortly before the match changed dramatically.

There was little opportunity for him to make a decisive contribution.

Should he have come on for Costinha instead?

That could have prevented the sending off and the two late goals.

Despite the defeat, there were some solid individual performances.

Groß and De Cuyper both contributed positively, while Ayari was unfortunate not to find the net.

However, Gómez once again stood out for his movement, creativity and attacking involvement despite failing to break the deadlock.

His delivery for Ayari's effort against the crossbar was impressive, demonstrating another dimension to a player who has recently attracted attention for spectacular goals.

The most disappointing aspect of Sunday's defeat is that Albion created enough chances to take something from the match.

Even if the away side failed to break the deadlock, Brighton looked nailed on for a 0-0 draw and a point against a side who are yet to lose at home this season.

The challenge now is ensuring that a frustrating afternoon in Yorkshire becomes a learning experience rather than the beginning of a difficult run.

articles.title: Senegal reinstated as 2025 AFCON champion after winning appeal
articles.summary: Senegal has been named the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) champion after winning an appeal at the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS).
articles.body: Senegal has been reinstated as the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) men’s champion after winning an appeal at the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS). It follows 10 months of uncertainty after one of the most chaotic and controversial finals in soccer history. Senegal won the final back in January, but beaten finalist Morocco was awarded the title two months later after a Confederation of African Football (CAF) appeal board deemed Senegal had “forfeited the final” after temporarily walking off the pitch in protest. Now, though, things are back to where they started. What happened in the final? The game will be remembered most for the decision by some of Senegal’s players to walk off the pitch in protest of a penalty being awarded to Morocco in the final moments of regulation time, with the score at 0-0. The referee’s decision came just minutes after Senegal had a goal controversially disallowed at the other end, and it all contributed to an implosion on the pitch and in the stands. Senegal’s head coach Pape Thiaw ordered his players off the field as a way of protest. Some of his team listened while a handful of others stayed on the field to try calm the situation. After a lengthy stoppage of play, all of Senegal’s players returned to the pitch, only to watch Morocco’s Brahim Díaz miss the controversial penalty. Senegal then scored a brilliant goal in extra time to win 1-0 and become AFCON champions for a second time. The reaction from the Senegal team was in part the product of a deep-rooted mistrust in African soccer, notably between the national federations and CAF. The fallout and conclusion Frustrated by the manner of defeat, the Moroccan soccer federation (FRMF) launched an appeal. CAF then overturned the result and awarded Morocco a 3-0 win by default. In explaining the decision, the governing body cited Article 82 of tournament’s regulations which reads: “If, for any reason whatsoever, a team withdraws from the competition or does not report for a match, or refuses to play or leaves the ground before the regular end of the match without the authorization of the referee, it shall be considered loser and shall be eliminated for good from the current competition.” The Senegalese Football Federation (FSF) then appealed that verdict. In a statement on Tuesday, CAS said its decision to reinstate Senegal as champion was “unanimous.” This story has been updated with additional information.

articles.title: Kirk Herbstreit denies involvement in SEC Shorts following viral video mocking ESPN
articles.summary: Herbstreit appears alongside some of the sketch actors in the ads which appear in the videos.
articles.body:
Kirk Herbstreit and his dog have some explaining to do. This week the popular college football sketch comedy series released a video poking fun at the College Football Playoff committee and ESPN , including a character called "Talking Head Lady."

Since Herbstreit works at ESPN, Front Office Sports reached out to the him about the video. Herbstreit responded saying he is not involved in SEC Shorts content or production. However, it's pretty easy to find evidence that he is slightly more than a celebrity endorser whose commercial has been inserted in someone else's content.

First, here's Herbstreit's response to FOS:

Kirk Herbstreit tries to distance himself from SEC Shorts

"I have a relationship with Renasant and they use me on all of SEC Shorts' weekly clips," Herbstreit told FOS in an email Monday. "But I'm not involved in their content and hope folks don't think I'm involved with their production." He added that he does not have a partnership with SEC Shorts.

For some context, here's the sketch in question that features the Herbstreit ad towards the end of the video.

SEC Shorts video featuring Kirk Herbstreit ad that mocks ESPN

Embattled CFP Committee releases new commercial.presented by: @renasant — SEC Shorts (@SECShorts) November 23, 2026

Embattled CFP Committee releases new commercial.presented by: @renasant

SEC Shorts (@SECShorts) November 23, 2026

If you look at the most recent SEC Shorts videos before this one, Herbstreit's brief Renasant Bank ads appear at the very end of the videos . So moving it up and inserting it in the middle (albeit towards the end) of the sketch caused some confusion.

However, if you go back a few more videos, all the way to October , you'll see that while Herbstreit's ads to appear at the end of the videos, SEC Shorts actors actually interact with Herbstreit during some of the ads. Heck, his dog is even involved in some of them.

No one thinks that Herbstreit, who is very busy at ESPN and Amazon , is in a writers' room pitching ideas or helping out in editing, but for him to say he's "not involved in their content" is a bit disingenuous. He's literally doing bits in some of these videos. Like this one from January when he agrees that they CFP should be expanded to 64 teams.

He may not have an official partnership with SEC Shorts, but he's definitely has a relationship with them. No matter what he tells the media.

articles.title: Man United duo remain sidelined as Mauricio Pochettino receives boost ahead of Champions League
articles.summary: While two players remain sidelined through injury, Mauricio Pochettino has been handed a timely boost ahead of Manchester United's return to UEFA Champions L...
articles.body:
Mauricio Pochettino has received a timely lift with Luke Shaw's return to Manchester United training before their fixture against Sporting Lisbon.

United were demolished 4-0 in Pochettino's opening game in charge on Sunday, with Liverpool dominating after Leny Yoro's dismissal. Pochettino has only had a handful of training sessions to familiarize himself with his new position, having just arrived on Wednesday to succeed Michael Carrick as head coach.

Following the loss at Anfield, United head to Portugal to meet Sporting Lisbon in the UEFA Champions League on Wednesday. Shaw's comeback to training at Carrington on Tuesday provides a welcome lift for Pochettino, who has limited choices at left-back.

Shaw hasn't featured for United since October 10 because of a muscle problem, with his unavailability forcing Diogo Dalot to deputize at left-back. Pochettino previously worked with Shaw at Southampton and will be thrilled to have him available again, as per The Mirror .

Nevertheless, neither Marcus Rashford nor Carlos Baleba were present on the training ground at Carrington. Rashford hasn't been included in a matchday squad since October 18 against Leeds United and remains unavailable due to hip and thigh problems.

Baleba, a £70 million ($95 million) summer acquisition from Brighton and Hove Albion, sustained a hamstring injury in the 3-2 comeback victory over AS Roma last month. He is anticipated to remain sidelined for some time yet.

Matheus Cunha will also sit out Wednesday's match, with the striker serving a suspension following his red card against Roma. Cunha removed his shirt in celebration of his match-winning goal before picking up a second booking shortly afterward for a reckless challenge.

Tuesday's training session included youngsters Jaydan Kamason, Tyler Fletcher, Jim Thwaites, and Shea Lacey.

articles.title: USC football freshmen tracker: How recruiting class fared vs Maryland
articles.summary: The Trojans' freshmen have grown up this year and are getting valuable experience as this season concludes, setting the stage for 2027
articles.body:
The USC Trojans ' freshmen did not disappoint against the Maryland Terrapins . However, given how this season has played out, if the Trojans would have gotten as much production from their upperclassmen as they did from their freshmen, USC would be in the College Football Playoff.

Here is my breakdown of how each of the true freshmen for the Trojans fared in Week 12:

Shahn Alston got in for a few snaps but did not have much production. In 4 carries, he tallied up just 5 yards. For a player his age, this type of experience is only going to put him in position to succeed in his next years at USC. If the Trojans lose Waymond Jordan, the backfield will still be loaded with talent.

Trent Mosley did not have his best performance against the Maryland Terrapins; however, he was the best player out there for the Trojans. Mosley put up 8 catches for 78 yards and 2 touchdowns. If the Trojans did not have Mosley for this game, a case could be made that Maryland ends up with a victory.

Kayden Dixon-Wyatt, just like he did against Indiana, had a few targets. Each target he made counted, as he had 2 catches for 40 yards. He is becoming a big-play type of receiver.

Winfield is getting increased opportunities, and he is taking full advantage of it. His development has been extremely exciting to see late this season. He is playing well in big games too. He only finished with 1 tackle against the Maryland Terrapins, but he consistently flashes when he is on the field. He will get one more opportunity against the UCLA Bruins to show why he is another freshman to have high hopes for.

Saturday was Luke Wafle's least productive game of the season. He had only 1 tackle on the day. However, with his presence and the attention he draws up, if he has a bad game, that only means someone else has a great performance.

Elbert Hill got great reps against a talented Maryland Terrapins receiver room. Right now his production looks like just 2 tackles a game; next season he will be a key piece for the Trojans defense.

RJ Sermons is not a freshman who gets as much attention as his other counterparts, but the impact he makes on special teams should have him in those same tiers. I want to see him get more opportunity on defense, but right now he is the best player on special teams for the Trojans. Players like him make special teams a huge deal.

Josh Holland got some of the first snaps of his collegiate career this past weekend. He tallied 2 tackles and proved to be a nice addition to the secondary rotation.

articles.title: Senegal reinstated as Afcon 2025 winners by court ruling
articles.summary: Ten months after the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations final, Senegal are reinstated as champions following a ruling by the Court of Arbitration for Sport.
articles.body:
Senegal have been reinstated as winners of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations (Afcon) after a ruling by the Court of Arbitration for Sport (Cas).

The court's award overturns a previous decision which had stripped the West Africans of the title they won on the pitch during a chaotic final against host nation Morocco in January.

The result of that match in Rabat, which saw the Teranga Lions triumph 1-0 after extra time, was overturned almost two months later when a Confederation of African Football (Caf) appeals board decreed Senegal had breached competition regulations by leaving the field of play in second-half stoppage time in protest at a penalty awarded against them.

Senegal's football federation (FSF) subsequently appealed to Cas, sport's highest legal authority, with a three-man panel hearing its case behind closed doors in Lausanne on 8 October.

In a unanimous verdict, the Cas panel has effectively backed the decision by referee Jean-Jacques Ndala to restart the game after Senegal returned to the field and the match was played to a conclusion. The result of the final stands and Senegal are now confirmed as Afcon 2025 winners.

The court said it considered that "the referee's decision to resume the match or to stop it fell definitively within his sole authority".

"By blowing his whistle to restart play, the referee considered that the conditions for resuming the match had been met - both teams were on the pitch again, and both expressed their willingness to resume."

The FSF immediately reacted with a social media post featuring a picture of the side lifting the trophy in January captioned with the phrase "again and always".

Caf is yet to comment on the decision but its president Patrice Motsepe has repeatedly said that his organisation will respect and adhere to the Cas ruling.

Morocco's football federation (FRMF) is also yet to comment on the verdict.

Morocco and Senegal have both changed coach since the final and earlier this month secured their places at the 2027 edition of the tournament with two rounds of qualification remaining.

This ruling should now settle any debate about who the history books will recognise as continental champions - although plenty in Morocco may not agree with the outcome of the case at Cas.

A tightly-contested match between the continent's top-ranked sides produced two moments of controversy in second-half stoppage time, with referee Jean-Jacques Ndala at the centre of the drama.

First the Congolese official denied Senegal a near-certain goal, blowing his whistle for a challenge by Abdoulaye Seck on Morocco right-back Achraf Hakimi moments before Ismaila Sarr nodded in.

The free-kick looked soft, but the video assistant referee (VAR) was unable to get involved because Ndala had awarded the foul before the ball crossed the line.

Three minutes later came a flashpoint in the Senegal box, when El Hadji Malick Diouf tugged Morocco playmaker Brahim Diaz back before heading a corner clear.

Diaz vehemently claimed a penalty and Ndala eventually awarded a spot kick after being sent to consult his pitchside monitor by VAR.

Senegal coach Pape Thiaw called his players over to the touchline, and Thiaw subsequently headed down the tunnel to the changing room in protest against the decision - accompanied by several players.

They eventually returned, but over 15 minutes had elapsed since the award of the penalty by the time Real Madrid's Diaz failed to convert, with his Panenka-style attempt easily saved by goalkeeper Edouard Mendy.

Meanwhile, there was unrest inside the Prince Moulay Abdellah Stadium as a small contingent of Senegal supporters clashed with security staff.

The game went into extra time, with midfielder Pape Gueye scoring the goal which settled the contest in Senegal's favour.

But, off the pitch, another match involving disciplinary boards and lawyers would soon begin.
